title: From SDET to AI quality engineer
objectives: Distinguish testing with AI from testing AI
Map existing SDET skills to probabilistic systems
Identify the evidence needed to release an AI feature
relevance: You already understand contracts, coverage, regression, and release risk. AI extends these skills to systems where valid answers can vary between runs.

sections.title: Two tracks, one engineering mindset
paragraphs: Track A uses AI to improve software testing: generating API test candidates, classifying CI failures, or proposing missing edge cases. The generated artifacts still need review and deterministic execution.

Track B tests the AI application itself: whether a chatbot stays grounded, whether retrieval finds the right document, and whether an agent calls an authorized tool. Treat its output as evidence to evaluate, not a trustworthy oracle.

sections.title: Deterministic contracts, probabilistic behavior
paragraphs: A REST endpoint may promise an exact status code and schema. A chatbot can express the same correct answer in many ways. Separate hard invariants (valid JSON, no forbidden tool, citation points to supplied evidence) from quality rubrics (helpfulness, completeness, groundedness).

Freeze representative test inputs and application versions. Run repeated samples when variation matters. Record outputs, scores, cost, latency, and failure categories. One passing response is not proof of reliability.

sections.title: Your learning path
paragraphs: Build Python, data, SQL, and statistical foundations before abstractions. Then learn embeddings and retrieval before RAG frameworks; tool calling before agents; evaluation before release.

An AI engineer assembles useful model-powered systems. An ML engineer develops model training and serving pipelines. A data scientist investigates data and experiments. An AI quality engineer designs evidence and controls across those systems. Roles overlap; judge work by its purpose.

mistake: Using exact text equality for every LLM response rejects good paraphrases and misses groundedness failures.
takeaway: Preserve deterministic invariants and measure uncertain behavior across a representative dataset.

title: A reproducible engineering workspace
objectives: Isolate dependencies in a virtual environment
Separate experiments from production modules
Keep secrets out of browser applications
relevance: A reproducible lab turns a notebook experiment into a testable CI artifact that colleagues can run.

sections.title: An environment is part of the program
paragraphs: Use a project-specific virtual environment. Select its interpreter in VS Code. Keep dependency declarations in the repository and record the Python version in your README. A package imported from your global machine can hide a missing dependency.

A notebook is useful for inspecting data and plots. Move durable logic into importable modules with tests. Git should track source and small synthetic datasets, not virtual environments or secret files.
sections.code:
python -m venv .venv
# Linux / macOS
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install pytest
python -m pytest

sections.title: Static safe mode and local labs
paragraphs: The course executes educational Python and SQL in your browser. It has no provider key and no model API requirement. Optional local labs use a Python process on your machine.

A browser bundle is downloadable by every visitor. An environment variable prefixed for Vite client use is still public after bundling. Keep provider credentials exclusively in local processes or a properly authenticated server.

import os
api_key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
# Never print api_key or commit a populated .env file.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A notebook is useful for inspecting one experiment, but execution order can hide dependencies: a cell may succeed only because an earlier cell created a variable. Move the analyzer into an importable function and run it from a fresh interpreter. Keep a small notebook as a consumer of that function rather than a second implementation.

Use a virtual environment per project and install from a reviewed manifest. Record Python and package versions with the run artifact; a requirements range alone does not recreate a particular installation. Store a tested lock or freeze after validation. Verify setup with an import smoke test and the analyzer's behavior tests before connecting a provider. A key belongs in the local process environment and must be excluded from Git, browser bundles and progress backups.

mistake: Committing .env or putting a provider key into a VITE_ variable exposes the secret.
takeaway: A clean checkout plus documented setup should reproduce your test results.

title: Define an AI release contract
objectives: Define an AI release contract
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects define an ai release contract with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Build a small suite with an allowed request, a forbidden request, an unanswerable question, and a valid paraphrase.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An AI feature is a system of deterministic boundaries around probabilistic inference. A useful release contract separates hard constraints from graded usefulness: a tool must never read another tenant’s logs, while a summary may be correct in several phrasings. Model quality cannot compensate for an unauthorized action.

Write a risk register before selecting a framework. Identify who can be harmed, the action scope, evidence sources, uncertainty tolerance, and fallback. An AI quality engineer collaborates on these product decisions rather than merely choosing an evaluator after implementation.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Represent each invariant as an executable predicate and each graded requirement as a documented rubric. Version the dataset, prompt, model, retriever, and policy with the run. Compare matched cases and retain per-case evidence instead of storing only an average.

A project README should distinguish observations on synthetic data from production claims. Define who adjudicates uncertain outputs and how a release can be rolled back. The risk contract becomes acceptance criteria for the learner’s portfolio.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A score of 92% can hide a single severe cross-tenant failure. Segment the report by risk and prohibit aggregation from overriding critical gates. A model refusal is not automatically correct: an authorized, answerable request may have been refused unnecessarily.

Reproduce the request using its exact versions, check the authorization decision, and inspect evidence passed to the model. Determine whether the defect is a broken deterministic boundary or an uncertain response.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Build a small suite with an allowed request, a forbidden request, an unanswerable question, and a valid paraphrase. Record contract compliance separately from usefulness. Show which boundary prevented a forbidden action and which rubric scored the paraphrase.

The release review should include failures, confidence limits, and operating budgets. An SDET’s regression mindset becomes especially valuable when every model upgrade can change behavior without changing application code.

exercise.solution: Authorize tenant access before retrieval, validate the response schema, and reject forbidden tool proposals. Evaluate grounded summaries on a versioned dataset using a calibrated rubric. On outage return a deterministic evidence-only report and retain rollback versions.

title: Values, collections, and API contracts
objectives: Choose the right collection for a test result
Understand mutable objects and missing fields
Normalize external values at a contract boundary
relevance: Test reports and API responses arrive as nested data. The first quality boundary is explicit, predictable normalization.

sections.title: Python values are objects
paragraphs: Names bind to objects; they are not storage boxes with fixed types. Integers, floats, strings, booleans, and None represent distinct meanings. The string "false" is truthy because it is non-empty. Never convert an API flag with bool(raw) when raw might be a string.

Lists preserve order and allow mutation; tuples represent fixed ordered records; dictionaries map keys to values; sets store unique hashable values. Choose a set for duplicate test IDs and a list for ordered execution results.

sections.title: Aliasing and boundary validation
paragraphs: Assigning a list to another name does not copy it. Mutating through either name changes the same object. A shallow copy only copies the outer collection; nested dictionaries still share identity.

Use direct indexing for a required field when absence is an error. Use .get for optional values only when a default has a defined meaning. Validate status values before computing pass rate; silently treating unknown status as pass corrupts metrics.
sections.code:
original = [{"status": "failed"}]
copy = original.copy()
copy[0]["status"] = "passed"
print(original[0]["status"])  # passed

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A dictionary maps stable test IDs to records; a set records membership such as already-seen IDs; a list preserves an ordered event stream. Choosing a set for the event stream discards ordering and duplicates, which can hide repeated failures. A tuple can represent a fixed composite identity such as tenant, build and test.

Mutability matters when fixtures are shared. Assigning second = first does not copy a list, and a shallow dictionary copy still shares nested lists. A test that appends to a nested fixture can change later tests. Build a fresh fixture for each test or copy the exact mutable boundary. Test duplicates, absent keys and unexpected field types, and avoid using a mutable default argument such as failures=[] in a function signature.

mistake: A shallow list copy still shares nested dictionaries.
takeaway: Model the data contract before transforming the data.

exercise.explanation: The copied list references the same inner dictionary. Use a deep copy or construct new records when isolation is needed.

title: Filter, transform, and summarize test runs
objectives: Use loops and comprehensions for explicit transformations
Implement a pure function with clear return values
Handle empty inputs deliberately
relevance: A small pure analyzer is easier to unit test than a script that reads files, mutates globals, and prints everything.

sections.title: From API response to useful evidence
paragraphs: An if statement branches by a condition. A for loop iterates over objects directly. A comprehension expresses a simple filter and transformation together; keep complex business decisions in a named function.
A function should have an explicit contract: inputs, output shape, and exceptional cases. Parameters are local names. return sends a value to the caller; print only writes a display message.
sections.code:
runs = [{"name": "login", "status": "failed"},
        {"name": "search", "status": "passed"}]
failed = [r["name"] for r in runs if r["status"] == "failed"]
print(failed)

sections.title: Empty input and scope
paragraphs: A pass rate for no test executions is undefined; return None or raise a domain error rather than claiming 100%. Use type hints to communicate that possibility.

Avoid hidden globals and mutable default arguments. A default list is created once when the function is defined, so repeated calls can unintentionally share state. Use None and create a new list inside the function.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A comprehension is a transformation, not a substitute for readable error handling. Collect failed records with a clear predicate, then compute summaries separately. If a status is missing, decide explicitly whether to reject the record or label it unknown; silently treating it as passed changes the denominator.

Short-circuit operators return operands, which can be useful but surprising: value or default replaces valid falsy values such as zero. A zero duration is different from a missing duration. Use is None when absence is the intended condition. Test an empty run list, all passes, all failures, missing fields and zero durations. These cases establish the analyzer's contract independently of the large synthetic dataset.

mistake: A function that prints a result but never returns it gives the caller None.
takeaway: Pure transformations let you test the contract independently of files and APIs.

title: Functions, arguments, and maintainable modules
objectives: Use keyword-only arguments for important options
Understand module import behavior and scope
Separate I/O from transformation logic
relevance: Reusable test utilities need stable public interfaces and predictable imports.

sections.title: Design an explicit interface
paragraphs: Positional arguments fit obvious small inputs. Keyword-only arguments make policy visible at the call site: summarize(runs, slow_threshold=3.0). The * marker in a function signature makes following parameters keyword-only.
Local scope belongs to each function call. Read-only access to a global configuration can look convenient, but passing configuration makes tests independent and deterministic.

sections.title: Modules should be safe to import
paragraphs: A module executes its top-level statements when imported. Guard CLI entry points with if __name__ == "__main__" so imports do not read files or start network requests. Packages group related modules; keep core logic separate from transport and presentation.

Decorators wrap functions, so preserve metadata with functools.wraps. Generators yield values lazily and avoid holding every record in memory, but they are consumed once. Materialize a list if downstream operations need multiple passes.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: Function contracts should name accepted input, returned shape and failure behavior. A pure summarize function receives records and returns metrics without opening files or reading environment variables. A thin command-line wrapper owns file loading and report writing. This separation makes malformed-file tests different from aggregation tests.

Avoid global mutable counters and hidden configuration, because tests then depend on execution order. Use keyword-only arguments for optional policies such as unknown_status='reject', and document when an exception is raised. A decorator can add timing while preserving the wrapped function's metadata with functools.wraps, but it must return the result and propagate errors. Verify both success and failure paths after wrapping; observability should not change the domain contract.

mistake: Iterating over an exhausted generator again produces no values.
takeaway: Use explicit arguments and import-safe modules to keep test utilities reusable.

title: Types, validation, and error boundaries
objectives: Distinguish type hints from runtime validation
Represent domain records with dataclasses
Catch errors at the layer that can handle them
relevance: Invalid API data should fail at the boundary instead of creating misleading CI analytics.

sections.title: Type hints describe, validation enforces
paragraphs: A type hint helps tooling find incompatible calls; Python does not automatically reject a wrong runtime value. A dataclass reduces boilerplate for domain objects but also does not validate fields automatically.

Validate external JSON with explicit checks or a schema library such as Pydantic in local labs. Separate transport errors, parsing errors, and domain validation errors so a retry policy can distinguish temporary failures from bad requests.

sections.title: Reliable I/O and concurrency
paragraphs: Use pathlib for portable paths and context managers to guarantee file cleanup. Log event metadata without credentials or private payloads. JSON parsing is not schema validation.

async/await helps overlap I/O, not accelerate CPU work. Use bounded concurrency to avoid flooding a service. Propagate cancellation and set timeouts; broad except Exception plus an empty return makes service failures look like successful zero-result runs.
sections.code:
import json
from pathlib import Path

with Path("test-results.json").open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    records = json.load(stream)

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: Runtime validation must distinguish coercion from a strict contract. A duration supplied as the string '2.4' may be intentionally accepted by an ingestion adapter, but a tool's write approval should never interpret arbitrary nonempty strings as true. Validate boundaries according to the domain and preserve rejected records with safe error categories.

Use pathlib for explicit fixture roots and context managers for file handles. Validate parsed JSON structure after parsing: syntactically valid JSON can still be an array where a dictionary is required. Write reports to a temporary file and replace the target after the complete artifact is ready, preventing readers from observing partial output. Test missing files, invalid encoding, malformed JSON and valid-but-wrong types separately.

mistake: Catching every exception and returning [] hides outages as valid empty datasets.
takeaway: Validate at boundaries and preserve error meaning.

title: Test the analyzer, including what can break
objectives: Design boundary tests with pytest
Use parametrization and fixtures deliberately
Mock external dependencies at their boundary
relevance: Your existing SDET skills apply directly: test small functions deterministically and integration points separately.

sections.title: Useful tests specify behavior
paragraphs: pytest discovers test_ functions and reports assertion differences. Parametrization describes a set of cases without duplicated code. A fixture owns setup and cleanup; avoid session-scoped mutable objects that leak state between tests.
Test empty input, one record, mixed outcomes, duplicate test names, invalid duration, and ties in slowest tests. A passing line-coverage target does not prove these behaviors.

sections.title: Mocks and properties
paragraphs: Mock the HTTP client, not the internal implementation you want to test. monkeypatch can replace environment values or functions for one test. Test real schema validation against malformed synthetic API responses.

A property is an invariant over many inputs: the failure count is between zero and total count; reordering results should not change a rate. Property-based tests generate cases to challenge those invariants, complementing carefully chosen examples.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A useful test must fail when the behavior it protects is broken. For the analyzer, independently compute a tiny expected result rather than calling the same helper used by production code to create the expectation. Change failed to passed in one input and confirm only the intended count changes.

Parametrize boundary cases and use fixtures to provide fresh records. Monkeypatch environment variables and mock network adapters at the application's dependency boundary, not inside the function under test. Property-based testing can generate many inputs for invariants such as 0 <= pass_rate <= 1 and failure_count <= total_count, but those invariants do not prove the exact formula. Combine broad properties with hand-computed examples and targeted counterexamples.

mistake: A mock that returns the same answer the implementation expects can pass while the real integration is broken.
takeaway: Test behavior at boundaries and use properties to explore more inputs.

title: Bounded async, cancellation, and retry
objectives: Bounded async, cancellation, and retry
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects bounded async, cancellation, and retry with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Exercise a bounded fetcher with slow, successful, transient, and permanent responses.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Async functions suspend at await so other tasks can progress during I/O. They do not turn CPU-heavy parsing into parallel computation. Blocking a model SDK or file transform inside an async route can still stall every concurrent request.

Concurrency should be a budget: use a semaphore to bound outstanding API calls and define a deadline for the whole operation. A generator yields records lazily; an async generator can stream observations without retaining an entire report.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use async with for locks and resource lifetimes. asyncio.wait_for bounds a coroutine and cancels it on timeout; propagate cancellation rather than catching it as an ordinary successful result. Retry only classified transient errors within the original deadline.

Decorators can add timing while functools.wraps preserves names and metadata. Keep retry/timing wrappers separate from business transformation. Test both the returned values and whether cancellation closes the underlying resource.
sections.code:
import asyncio
async def collect(items, fetch, limit=2):
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(limit)
    async def one(item):
        async with sem:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(fetch(item), 2)
    return await asyncio.gather(*(one(x) for x in items))

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Unbounded gather over thousands of CI logs can exhaust sockets and trigger rate limits. A synchronous sleep in an async retry blocks the event loop; use asyncio.sleep. Repeated retries with a fresh timeout can exceed the user’s overall request budget.

Inject a fake clock or zero delay and a fake transport for tests. Count attempts, assert a permanent error is not retried, and check cancellation leaves no background write. Do not retry a non-idempotent action without an idempotency contract.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Exercise a bounded fetcher with slow, successful, transient, and permanent responses. Measure maximum simultaneous calls, total deadline, and abandoned work. Testing concurrency is about observable contracts rather than an exact scheduler order.

This applies to Playwright API checks, batched log analysis, provider requests, and future agent tools. A good interview explanation names the independent I/O work and the enforced concurrency budget.

mistake: Unbounded gather over thousands of CI logs can exhaust sockets and trigger rate limits. A synchronous sleep in an async retry blocks the event loop; use asyncio.sleep. Repeated retries with a fresh timeout can exceed the user’s overall request budget.
takeaway: Exercise a bounded fetcher with slow, successful, transient, and permanent responses.

assert not retryable(400) and not retryable(200)

title: Classes, enums, Pydantic, and contract testing
objectives: Classes, enums, Pydantic, and contract testing
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects classes, enums, pydantic, and contract testing with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Keep request, response, and internal state models distinct so a response cannot leak private transport fields.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Classes group state and behavior; a dataclass is convenient for an internal record, and an enum restricts named domain choices. Inheritance can model a stable substitutable interface, but composition is usually clearer for a transport, validator, and reporter.

Static types assist review and tools. External JSON still needs runtime validation. Pydantic models can enforce bounds and forbid extra fields; strict behavior must be selected deliberately because coercion can otherwise accept a string where a number was intended.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Create a request model with a bounded log, explicit category enum, and strict duration. Use model_validate at the API boundary and model_dump for serialization. Use field validators for rules that involve more than basic types.

In tests, parameterize valid and invalid requests. A fixture constructs a new service per test; monkeypatch replaces environment values without leaking them to the next test. Mock an adapter protocol so schema validation and business logic remain real.
sections.code:
from enum import Enum
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class Status(str, Enum):
    passed="passed"
    failed="failed"
class Result(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    name: str = Field(min_length=1)
    status: Status
    duration: float = Field(ge=0, strict=True)

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A unit mock that returns prevalidated domain objects bypasses the dangerous parsing boundary. Include integration cases with missing keys, extra keys, negative values, booleans in numeric fields, and invalid enums. Property tests verify invariants over generated records.

A marker can separate network integration tests, but excluding all of them forever is not a quality strategy. Know which tests ran, and retain one meaningful adapter contract check with synthetic payloads.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Keep request, response, and internal state models distinct so a response cannot leak private transport fields. Test serialization and exception mapping as part of the public API contract. Demonstrate a fixture’s cleanup with a failing test.
This pattern transfers directly to REST/GraphQL contract testing and structured AI output. A valid schema is necessary, but it cannot establish that a predicted defect category is factually correct.

mistake: A unit mock that returns prevalidated domain objects bypasses the dangerous parsing boundary. Include integration cases with missing keys, extra keys, negative values, booleans in numeric fields, and invalid enums. Property tests verify invariants over generated records.
takeaway: Keep request, response, and internal state models distinct so a response cannot leak private transport fields.

title: Files, structured logs, and streaming reports
objectives: Files, structured logs, and streaming reports
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects files, structured logs, and streaming reports with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Build a CLI report containing accepted rows, rejected rows, failure frequency, and duration summaries.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: pathlib makes path composition explicit across operating systems. JSON preserves nested records; CSV represents rows and needs a defined dialect, schema, and encoding. Environment variables configure processes without committing secrets.

A context manager owns cleanup even when parsing fails. Iterators and generators let a result analyzer process large histories incrementally, but consumers must understand that a stream is exhausted after iteration.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Separate reading from transformation and writing. Open files with encoding=utf-8 and newline="" for CSV. Validate rows as they are read and retain rejected-row counts. Emit JSON logs containing event, run_id, stage, and outcome; redact log bodies and credentials.

Write reports atomically: create a temporary sibling file, flush it, then replace the final path. A crash should leave either the previous complete report or the new one, rather than a partially written artifact.
sections.code:
import csv
from pathlib import Path
def rows(path):
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        yield from csv.DictReader(stream)
# list(rows("datasets/test-runs.csv"))

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A relative path can refer to a different directory in CI than in VS Code. Anchor fixture paths to the repository or require an explicit CLI argument. Logging the entire environment can expose provider credentials.

A reused generator can produce an empty second metric pass. Aggregate in one pass or deliberately materialize bounded input. Test a corrupt row halfway through a stream and verify cleanup and error reporting.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Build a CLI report containing accepted rows, rejected rows, failure frequency, and duration summaries. Make exit status nonzero for violated ingestion policy so GitHub Actions can block the pipeline. Keep ordinary empty input distinguishable from a failed read.
The same boundaries support dataset ingestion, evaluation artifacts, and incident reports. An SDET should be able to reproduce an artifact from a clean checkout and explain every excluded record.

mistake: A relative path can refer to a different directory in CI than in VS Code. Anchor fixture paths to the repository or require an explicit CLI argument. Logging the entire environment can expose provider credentials.

title: Arrays, shapes, and vectorized metrics
objectives: Interpret array shape and axes
Use boolean masks and aggregation
Understand broadcasting instead of guessing
relevance: Embedding batches and latency metrics use array operations. A wrong axis gives plausible but incorrect quality reports.

sections.title: Shape describes your contract
paragraphs: A NumPy ndarray stores typed values in a multidimensional shape. A matrix shaped (runs, tests) has one row per run. sum(axis=0) reduces the run axis and produces one value per test. sum(axis=1) produces one value per run.
Vectorized operations apply across arrays efficiently. A boolean mask selects observations. Slices can share memory with the original array, so use .copy() when mutation should be isolated.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
passed = np.array([[1, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0]])
print(passed.shape)  # (2, 3)
print(passed.mean(axis=0))  # rate for each test

sections.title: Broadcasting rules
paragraphs: NumPy compares trailing dimensions. Dimensions match when equal or when one is 1. An array of shape (3,) can be added to (2, 3); an array of shape (2,) cannot without reshaping to (2, 1).

The result may be valid mathematically but wrong semantically. Label axes before operations. Explicitly choose floating-point dtype before division or normalization; integer storage can truncate derived values.
sections.code:
latency = np.array([[100., 200., 300.], [120., 220., 330.]])
baseline = np.array([100., 200., 300.])
print(latency / baseline)

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: For a duration table shaped [builds, tests], axis=0 aggregates across builds and axis=1 aggregates across tests. Keep axis names in comments or variable names because an array does not retain the meaning of its coordinates automatically. A scalar, row vector and column vector have different broadcasting behavior.

Boolean masks select elements satisfying a condition; using a mask with the wrong shape can fail or select the wrong subset. Check dtype and finite values before computing statistics. Integer arrays are appropriate for IDs but floating-point arrays are needed for normalized metrics. Test a one-row table, a one-column table, empty arrays and NaN values. Compare vectorized output with a small explicit loop as an independent oracle.

mistake: Broadcasting a baseline along the wrong axis silently compares unrelated observations.
takeaway: Write the meaning of each axis alongside its shape.

title: Cosine similarity from first principles
objectives: Compute dot product and vector norms
Distinguish direction from magnitude
Handle zero vectors explicitly
relevance: Semantically similar failures may have different text. Vector similarity is a useful candidate signal, but it is not proof of the same root cause.

sections.title: A vector is a representation
paragraphs: A vector is an ordered list of numeric coordinates. An embedding model learns representations whose geometry can capture useful relationships. The synthetic vectors in this lab are hand-designed for arithmetic practice; they are not real semantic embeddings.

The dot product sums pairwise coordinate products. A norm measures length. Cosine similarity divides the dot product by both lengths, so it compares direction. Cosine 1 means the same direction; 0 is orthogonal; -1 is opposite.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([1., 2., 0.])
b = np.array([2., 4., 0.])
print(np.dot(a, b))  # 10
print(np.linalg.norm(a))  # sqrt(5)

sections.title: Normalization and distance
paragraphs: A unit vector is v / norm(v). For unit vectors the dot product equals cosine similarity. Squared Euclidean distance between unit vectors is 2 - 2*cosine, so they induce the same ranking. Unnormalized dot product also rewards magnitude.
A zero vector has no direction, so cosine is undefined. Reject it or apply a documented fallback. Do not divide by zero and hope NaN sorting will produce sensible retrieval results.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: Raw dot product rewards magnitude as well as direction. For a=[1,0], b=[10,1] and c=[1,0], b has a larger dot product than c but lower cosine similarity. This difference matters when an index is configured for dot distance while embeddings are not normalized.

A zero vector has no direction. The teaching implementation returns a declared zero score, while another application may reject it; either policy must be explicit and tested. Reject mismatched dimensions rather than letting zip silently truncate coordinates. In retrieval, keep document identity aligned with vector rows, and test identical, opposite, orthogonal and zero vectors. Geometric similarity remains evidence for ranking, not proof that two failure causes are the same.

mistake: Vectors from different models or dimensions are not comparable, even if their text looks related.
takeaway: Similarity is a geometric candidate signal that still needs domain validation.

title: Sampling, masks, and reproducible experiments
objectives: Use a seeded random generator
Separate deterministic fixtures from statistical samples
Choose representative slices for evaluation
relevance: Reproducible synthetic CI history helps compare analyzer versions without depending on proprietary data.

sections.title: Random does not mean uncontrolled
paragraphs: Use np.random.default_rng(seed) and keep the seed with the experiment. A fixed seed helps reproduce one sample but does not prove stability across samples. Sample multiple seeds when estimating uncertainty.
A mask such as durations > 5 identifies slow observations; np.percentile returns a tail summary. The mean can hide a small group of severe outliers, so retain raw observations and relevant segments.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
durations = rng.lognormal(mean=1, sigma=0.5, size=100)
print(np.percentile(durations, 95))
print(durations[durations > 5].size)

sections.title: Representative samples
paragraphs: Sampling only successful production interactions creates survivorship bias. Include unsuccessful requests, rare categories, long inputs, empty retrieval, and adversarial inputs in separately labeled slices.
Keep training, tuning, and final evaluation samples separate. Changing a prompt repeatedly against the final evaluation set effectively trains your decisions on that set.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A random seed reproduces a pseudo-random sequence under a fixed implementation and data order; it does not make a sample representative. Uniform row sampling can underrepresent rare product defects or repeat many rows from one incident. Stratification preserves selected class proportions, while group sampling avoids splitting closely related incidents across partitions.

Report which sampling unit was used: run, test, incident or build. For uncertainty estimates over correlated runs, resample independent incidents rather than individual repeated observations. Keep a sealed holdout that was not inspected during iteration. Test that sampled IDs are valid, groups are disjoint where required and every necessary class has coverage. Reproducibility and representativeness are separate evaluation properties.

mistake: A fixed seed gives repeatability, not a guarantee that the sample represents production.
takeaway: Version both the sampling method and the resulting evaluation dataset.

title: Matrix shapes and normalized batch similarity
objectives: Matrix shapes and normalized batch similarity
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects matrix shapes and normalized batch similarity with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Vectorized scoring is useful for transparent exact-retrieval reference results.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Embedding search can score many documents at once with a matrix product. If queries have shape [q,d] and documents [n,d], normalize each row and multiply queries by documents transposed to obtain [q,n]. Each output row is one query's score against every document.

The shared dimension d is a contract, not a value that can be reshaped arbitrarily. A transpose changes axes; reshape reorganizes the same flat storage. Confusing them can return the right dimensions with the wrong numerical relationships.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Compute row norms with axis=1 and keepdims=True, then divide using a zero-safe output. This broadcasts one norm per row across its d coordinates. Matrix multiplication @ performs a dot product along the shared dimension; elementwise * does not aggregate.

For queries [[1,0],[0,1]] and documents [[1,0],[1,1]], normalized scores are [[1,.707],[0,.707]]. Test against the manual cosine calculation before trusting a large batch. Keep dtype and finite-value checks at the boundary.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
q=np.array([[1.,0.],[0.,1.]])
d=np.array([[1.,0.],[1.,1.]])
d=d/np.linalg.norm(d,axis=1,keepdims=True)
print(q@d.T)

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Normalizing the whole matrix by one global norm changes ranking assumptions. Dividing integer arrays in place can fail or truncate under an inappropriate dtype. An empty document collection requires a correctly shaped empty score matrix, not an index error.
Check dimension mismatch, zero rows, non-finite values and each result's query/document identity. Use small hand-computed matrices as an independent oracle.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Vectorized scoring is useful for transparent exact-retrieval reference results. Measure its runtime separately from embedding generation and compare numerical results with the single-vector implementation.

For SDETs, shapes and mathematical invariants are powerful tests: normalized nonzero rows have norm one, self-similarity is one and orthogonal similarity is zero. They can detect wrong axes without requiring a large model or provider account.

mistake: Normalizing the whole matrix by one global norm changes ranking assumptions. Dividing integer arrays in place can fail or truncate under an inappropriate dtype. An empty document collection requires a correctly shaped empty score matrix, not an index error.
takeaway: Vectorized scoring is useful for transparent exact-retrieval reference results.

For queries [[1,0],[0,1]] and documents [[1,0],[1,1]], normalized scores are [[1,.707],[0,.707]]. Test against the manual cosine calculation before trusting a large batch. Keep dtype and finite-value checks at the boundary.

Apply this mechanism to a synthetic incident in the shared fixture set. Preserve input/output identities so a reviewer can reproduce the result. Use the earlier lessons' implementation checks rather than assuming the checkpoint example is correct.

print(q@d.T)

title: Clean test history without hiding defects
objectives: Inspect DataFrame schema and missing values
Distinguish duplicates from legitimate retries
Define missing-value policies before aggregation
relevance: A polished CI dashboard is misleading if ingestion silently drops flaky retries or imputes missing outcomes as success.

sections.title: Inspect before transforming
paragraphs: A DataFrame is a labeled table; each column is a Series. Start with head(), info(), dtypes, and isna().sum(). Read CSV with explicit types when identifiers have leading zeros. Parse timestamps with a defined timezone.
Selecting df["duration"] gives a Series; df[["duration"]] gives a DataFrame. Use .loc for explicit row and column selection. Copy a filtered slice before modifying it when isolation is required.
sections.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame([
    {"test": "login", "build": 1, "status": "failed", "duration": 4.5},
    {"test": "login", "build": 2, "status": "passed", "duration": None},
])
print(df.isna().sum())
print(df.loc[df["status"] == "failed", ["test", "build"]])

sections.title: Missing and duplicate records
paragraphs: A missing duration should remain unknown for latency analysis, not become zero. A missing status should be quarantined or counted separately. Preserve the denominator used in every metric.

Deduplicate by the ingestion identity, not merely by test name. Two executions of the same test in one build can be intentional retries. A stable key might include build_id, test_id, attempt, and environment. Keep raw data and document every cleaning decision.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: Missing data needs a domain interpretation before imputation. A missing duration may indicate a cancelled test; filling it with zero can make an outage look like a performance improvement. Preserve a missingness indicator and distinguish not-run from passed. Stable test IDs are safer join keys than display names that may be renamed.

Check duplicates on the intended identity, such as tenant, build and test, rather than dropping identical rows indiscriminately. A legitimate rerun has a different run ID and may be required to measure flakiness. Preserve raw records, clean in a reproducible function and count rejected or changed rows. Test malformed durations, duplicate identities and missing statuses, and verify that cleaning does not silently change the total population used for pass-rate metrics.

takeaway: Data cleaning must preserve the events that explain quality problems.

title: Pass rates and flaky-test analysis
objectives: Aggregate by meaningful groups
Keep run rate separate from test rate
Use mixed outcomes as evidence, not a verdict
relevance: A test that both passes and fails is a triage candidate. Confirm controlled conditions before labeling it flaky.

sections.title: Groupby makes the denominator explicit
paragraphs: Create a passed indicator and take its mean within each test group. This measures run-level pass rate. A test-level report answers a different question: how many distinct tests exhibit a behavior? Name the denominator in your report.

A mixed-outcome test has at least one pass and one fail in the observation window. Different code versions, environments, or test data can explain that pattern. Analyze repeated runs under comparable conditions before asserting nondeterministic flakiness.
sections.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({"test": ["login", "login", "search"],
                   "status": ["failed", "passed", "passed"]})
df["passed"] = df["status"].eq("passed")
print(df.groupby("test")["passed"].mean())

sections.title: Build a CI health report
paragraphs: Aggregate counts, median duration, and p95 by module and build. Retain failed-first-attempt rate separately from eventual pass rate so retries cannot hide instability.

Sort by impact, not merely count: consider failure frequency, business criticality, added retry time, and reproducibility. Use pivot tables for build-by-module summaries and convert timestamps before resampling.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A per-module pass rate needs the correct denominator. Excluding cancelled or missing-status rows may be a defensible policy, but report that exclusion; otherwise a module with many unexecuted tests can appear healthy. Weighted overall pass rate differs from the mean of module rates when modules have different numbers of runs.

Flakiness is not simply any test that ever failed. A candidate may show mixed pass/fail outcomes under comparable builds, but environment changes and product fixes can also explain the variation. Group by stable test identity, order by time and retain build context. Test all-pass, all-fail, mixed outcomes and one-run tests. Label the result a flaky-test candidate until the controlled reproduction establishes nondeterministic behavior.

mistake: A test passing after a retry is not evidence that its original failure was harmless.
takeaway: Report first-attempt outcomes and retries separately.

title: Joins, time windows, and regression signals
objectives: Validate merge cardinality
Compare duration trends within a test
Avoid leakage from future observations
relevance: Bad joins duplicate failures; uncontrolled comparisons make harmless dataset changes look like performance regressions.

sections.title: A join is a cardinality contract
paragraphs: Join executions to test metadata by stable test_id. validate="many_to_one" asserts that each metadata key appears once. A many-to-many join multiplies matching rows and inflates counts; inspect unmatched keys with indicator=True.
Use a left join to retain unknown tests for investigation. An inner join silently removes records with missing metadata. Group by environment and build when comparing performance.
sections.code:
# runs.merge(cases, on="test_id", how="left",
#            validate="many_to_one", indicator=True)
import pandas as pd
runs = pd.DataFrame({"test_id": [1,1,2], "duration": [2.,3.,1.]})
cases = pd.DataFrame({"test_id": [1,2], "module": ["auth","search"]})
print(runs.merge(cases, on="test_id", validate="many_to_one"))

sections.title: Time is an ordering constraint
paragraphs: Sort within a test by timestamp before shift() or rolling(). Use lagged features when predicting a future failure; a rolling window that includes the outcome leaks future information.
For a latency trend, compare median and tail within stable workloads and report sample sizes. A different mix of tests can change overall mean even when each test has unchanged latency.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A many-to-many join multiplies rows. If a test appears twice in both tables, the joined result contains four combinations; a later mean or count can be wrong even though no exception occurred. Use validate='many_to_one' when enriching runs with a single testcase record, and inspect unmatched keys with an indicator column.

Parse timestamps with an explicit timezone and sort within the test group before calculating lagged duration features. Input row order is not a chronological guarantee. A future build's duration must not become a feature for an earlier prediction. Test duplicate enrichment keys, unmatched IDs, tied timestamps and timezone conversion. Compare row counts before and after the join and retain the reason for every intended change.

mistake: A duplicate metadata key can multiply execution rows without raising an error unless cardinality is checked.
takeaway: Assert join cardinality and align time before calculating trends.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A pivot table turns row observations into a labeled matrix after aggregation. Choose index, columns, values, and aggregation explicitly: module-by-build first-attempt failure rate differs from test-by-date mean duration. Missing cells mean no observation, not zero failures.

Parse timestamps to timezone-aware UTC before sorting or resampling. Daylight-saving changes and mixed local offsets can create ambiguous ordering. Keep categorical identifiers as categories only when their vocabulary and unknown-value policy are defined.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use pd.to_datetime(..., utc=True), sort by test and timestamp, then group and shift to build lagged features. Merge metadata with validate="many_to_one". A rolling feature for prediction must use observations strictly before the predicted run.

Prefer vectorized transforms and map for straightforward substitutions; apply is useful for complex row logic but can be slower and conceal type changes. Inspect dtypes after transformations and keep raw evidence immutable.

title: Query test runs with explicit semantics
objectives: Filter before grouping when appropriate
Distinguish WHERE from HAVING
Use NULL-aware aggregates
relevance: SQL lets you investigate CI and service evidence near its source, with clear relational contracts.

sections.title: Rows, filters, and groups
paragraphs: SELECT chooses expressions; FROM supplies relations; WHERE filters rows; GROUP BY forms groups; HAVING filters groups; ORDER BY orders the final result. Without ORDER BY, row order is not guaranteed.
COUNT(*) counts rows. COUNT(duration) counts non-NULL durations. AVG(duration) ignores NULL. SQL comparisons with NULL produce unknown; use IS NULL, not = NULL.
sections.code:
SELECT test_id, COUNT(*) AS runs,
       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failures
FROM test_runs
GROUP BY test_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY test_id;

sections.title: The browser database
paragraphs: The lab seeds fictional builds, test_cases, test_runs, failures, and defects in DuckDB-WASM. No server receives your SQL. You can inspect data with SELECT * FROM test_runs.

Use GROUP BY for counts by module, CASE for indicators, and HAVING for minimum sample size. A CTE gives an intermediate result a meaningful name. It improves readability but does not necessarily force materialization.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: WHERE filters rows before aggregation; HAVING filters groups after aggregation. COUNT(*) counts rows, while COUNT(duration) excludes NULL durations. AVG also ignores NULL, which can conceal missing execution data if the report does not include a missing count. Use CASE to make denominator policy explicit.

Ordering is a contract when comparing query output in a test. Without ORDER BY, a database may return equivalent rows in a different order. Test all-pass, all-fail and NULL-status cases with hand-computed expected rows. Relational models should use stable keys and constraints for builds, cases, runs and defects; a test display name is a useful label but a weak primary key when names can change.

mistake: COUNT(duration) can be smaller than COUNT(*) when duration is unknown.
takeaway: Make NULL behavior and denominators visible in every metric.

relevance: Defect correlation requires faithful event relationships. A bad join can fabricate a spike in product failures.

sections.title: Preserving evidence
paragraphs: INNER JOIN retains matching pairs only. LEFT JOIN retains every left row and fills absent right fields with NULL. RIGHT JOIN is the symmetric concept; it can usually be rewritten as a left join with reversed tables.

Filtering a right-hand column in WHERE after a left join can remove the unmatched rows and effectively behave like an inner join. Put the match restriction in ON when retaining all left rows is the goal.
sections.code:
SELECT tc.name, COUNT(tr.run_id) AS executions
FROM test_cases tc
LEFT JOIN test_runs tr ON tc.test_id = tr.test_id
GROUP BY tc.test_id, tc.name
ORDER BY tc.name;

sections.title: Correlation is not causal attribution
paragraphs: Join failures to defects using an explicit defect_id when available. A shared time window or module is weaker evidence; describe it as correlation. Multiple defects per failure need a linking table and deliberate counting of distinct failure IDs.

UNION removes duplicate rows; UNION ALL preserves them. Do not use UNION as a bandage for an incorrect join. Indexes and query plans help diagnose performance, but measure scanned rows and join cardinalities before guessing.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A LEFT JOIN retains every left-side record, but a WHERE predicate on a right-side column can remove unmatched rows and effectively turn the result into an inner join. Put matching conditions in ON when unmatched cases must remain visible, and explicitly decide how NULL evidence affects the report.

Use EXISTS for membership questions when joined detail rows would multiply results. UNION removes duplicate rows; UNION ALL preserves them and is appropriate only when duplicate events should count. Test one-to-many failures, unmatched defects and duplicate related records. Explain expected row cardinality before running the query, then compare actual counts. A plausible report number is not enough if the join changed the unit of analysis.

mistake: COUNT(*) after a left join counts the preserved unmatched row; count a right-hand ID for actual matches.
takeaway: Choose a join by the evidence you must preserve.

title: Latest results, ranks, and failure streaks
objectives: Use window functions without collapsing rows
Make ordering deterministic
Find latest execution per test with a CTE
relevance: Latest-state dashboards and consecutive-failure alerts depend on per-test ordering, not global timestamps.

sections.title: Windows preserve rows
paragraphs: GROUP BY reduces multiple rows to a group. A window function annotates each row using its partition. ROW_NUMBER() gives a unique sequence within a partition; RANK() gives ties the same rank and leaves gaps.
Use PARTITION BY test_id for independent sequences. Order by build_id DESC and run_id DESC to break ties deterministically. Filter row number in an outer query or QUALIFY.

sections.title: Lag and failure streaks
paragraphs: LAG(status) reads the previous row within the ordered partition; LEAD reads the next. Three consecutive executions failing is not always three consecutive builds: retries can add rows and missing builds create gaps.

Define a build-level status policy first, then check the current and previous two statuses plus consecutive build identifiers. Production build IDs may not be sequential; join to a build calendar or explicit sequence.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A latest-result query needs a deterministic tie break. ROW_NUMBER over partition by test_id order by build_id descending, run_id descending identifies one latest run; RANK can return several ties. LAG and LEAD preserve rows while accessing neighbors within the declared order.

Three failures in a row is different from three failures anywhere in history. Filter-free ordered windows must preserve intervening passes; filtering failures before LAG creates a false streak. Tests with F,P,F,F and F,F,F make the distinction visible. Inspect plans to understand scans, sorts and joins, and evaluate indexes for the actual filter/order workload rather than assuming an index always improves performance.

mistake: Ordering only by timestamp when timestamps tie makes the selected latest row unstable.
takeaway: Define the unit of sequence and provide a stable tie breaker.

title: Subqueries, CASE, UNION, and query plans
objectives: Subqueries, CASE, UNION, and query plans

relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects subqueries, case, union, and query plans with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Verify a regression query against hand-calculated expected output and test tie ordering.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A correlated subquery references an outer row and can express existence without multiplying it. EXISTS asks whether at least one related row matches; a join returns all matching pairs. Choose based on the desired cardinality, then inspect the actual plan.

CASE models conditional expressions, UNION deduplicates result rows, and UNION ALL preserves events. Deduplication is not a repair for an incorrect join. Relational modeling separates stable test identity, builds, executions, and failure annotations.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use EXPLAIN to inspect operators and EXPLAIN ANALYZE when it is safe to execute the query. Examine filters, estimated and actual rows, join cardinality, and scan cost. Index usefulness depends on the engine and workload; do not assume an OLTP B-tree rule applies unchanged to DuckDB analytical scans.
For consecutive build failures, first reduce retries to a documented build-level outcome. Then LAG and LEAD operate over the build sequence. Require adjacency rather than merely three failed rows.

WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM test_runs tr

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An inner join drops unknown test metadata. A many-to-many join fabricates additional failure events. Selecting MAX(status) does not select the status associated with the latest timestamp.

Construct a fixture with duplicate metadata, missing builds, and multiple attempts. Compare row counts after every CTE. Query performance diagnoses should explain work performed, not just whether a query appears short.

SQL interviews reward explicit NULL and cardinality reasoning. In an AI evaluation store, incorrect joins can produce an apparent model improvement by silently dropping difficult cases.

title: Consecutive failures: preserve passes in the window
objectives: Consecutive failures
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects consecutive failures: preserve passes in the window with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. In the bundled nine-run fixture, checkout fails in all three builds and should be returned once.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Three failures somewhere in history do not prove three consecutive failing builds. Order every outcome by build and run identity, including passes, then inspect neighbors. Filtering to failed rows before a window calculation removes the events that interrupt a streak.
Define how reruns within a build are handled before counting consecutive builds. A latest-run policy can select one outcome per test/build; the streak then operates over those selected outcomes.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: First rank reruns by run_id descending within test/build and select row one. On the remaining complete history, calculate LAG(status,1) and LAG(status,2) partitioned by test_id and ordered by build_id. Select rows where all three statuses are failed.

For strict adjacent build IDs, also compare the lagged build IDs to current minus one and two. If a test was not scheduled in an intervening build, decide whether that missing observation breaks the streak and record the rule.
sections.code:
WITH history AS (
 SELECT test_id,status,build_id,
 LAG(status,1) OVER(PARTITION BY test_id ORDER BY build_id) AS prev,
 LAG(status,2) OVER(PARTITION BY test_id ORDER BY build_id) AS prev2
 FROM test_runs
) SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM history h JOIN test_cases c USING(test_id)
WHERE h.status='failed' AND prev='failed' AND prev2='failed' ORDER BY c.name;

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A query counts F,P,F,F as a three-failure streak after removing P. Another treats builds 1,4,8 as consecutive merely because they are adjacent observed rows.

Use tiny histories to test uninterrupted failures, intervening passes, missing builds and duplicate reruns. Inspect ordering and partition keys when results appear plausible but disagree with the declared policy.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: In the bundled nine-run fixture, checkout fails in all three builds and should be returned once. Login has two failures followed by a pass, and search has one failure between passes.

SDETs should compare exact expected names and explain why each excluded test does not meet the rule. Keep this query as a regression detector, not a claim that all repeated failures have the same root cause.

title: Distributions, percentiles, and misleading averages
objectives: Distinguish population from sample
Use median and p95 for skewed latency
Understand variance and standard deviation
relevance: Reliability reports need to describe the customer experience beyond a single average.

sections.title: Location and spread
paragraphs: The population is the full set you care about; a sample is the subset you observe. The mean adds values and divides by count. The median is the midpoint after sorting. A few long timeouts can raise the mean far above most requests.

Variance summarizes squared deviations from the mean; standard deviation returns to the original unit. Sample variance commonly uses n-1 to estimate population variance. Percentiles summarize tails, but estimates depend on sample size and interpolation policy.
sections.code:
import statistics
latency = [100, 110, 120, 125, 900]
print(statistics.mean(latency))  # 271
print(statistics.median(latency))  # 120

sections.title: Measure the distribution, not just one number
paragraphs: Latency is often right-skewed: many fast responses and a few slow ones. A normal-distribution assumption may be a poor fit. Plot or inspect the observed distribution before choosing a method.

A p95 from 20 requests is fragile. Report sample count, workload, measurement window, and error rate. Excluding timeouts improves reported latency while hiding the worst outcomes; report them separately and state the censoring policy.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: Mean and median describe center, while variance and standard deviation describe spread. Percentiles describe thresholds in an ordered sample under a stated convention. A latency report should include sample count, failure count and tail statistics because dropping timed-out requests can make an outage appear faster.

Population variance divides by N when describing the full declared population; sample variance often uses N−1 when estimating population variance under appropriate assumptions. Neither formula fixes a biased sample. Compare cold and warm requests, input lengths and concurrency before attributing a latency shift to a model change. Use a small hand-computed sample to test calculations and retain raw durations for investigating tail events.

mistake: An average latency improvement can coexist with a worse tail and more timeouts.
takeaway: Report central tendency, spread, tails, and failure count together.

title: Conditional probability and base rates
objectives: Distinguish P(alert|defect) from P(defect|alert)
Use base rates when interpreting classifiers
Recognize dependence between repeated outcomes
relevance: A failure triage model with impressive recall can still overwhelm engineers with false alerts when product defects are rare.

sections.title: A probability needs a denominator
paragraphs: P(A|B) is the probability of A among cases where B occurred. It differs from P(B|A). Recall asks how many actual defects were flagged; precision asks how many flags were actual defects.

Suppose 1% of 10,000 failures are product defects. A detector catches 90 of 100 defects and falsely flags 5% of the 9,900 others, or 495 cases. Precision is 90/(90+495), about 15.4%, despite 90% recall.

sections.title: Bernoulli and binomial models
paragraphs: A single binary outcome can be modeled as Bernoulli with probability p. The binomial counts successes in n independent trials with the same p. These assumptions matter: repeated chatbot turns from the same conversation can be correlated.

Repeated flaky-test runs under shared infrastructure may fail together during an outage. Treating them as independent evidence produces overly narrow confidence intervals. Resample or analyze at the independent unit, such as build or conversation.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: Suppose only 1% of runs are true product defects, a detector finds 90% of them, and it alerts on 5% of non-defects. Among 10,000 runs, about 90 alerts are true positives and 495 are false positives, so positive predictive value is only 90/585, about 15.4%. High sensitivity does not imply trustworthy alerts when the base rate is low.

Conditional probabilities depend on what is being conditioned on: P(alert|defect) differs from P(defect|alert). Bernoulli models describe one binary outcome and binomial models count independent trials with a common success probability. Related CI retries violate independence, so choose the sampling unit carefully. Test the Bayes calculation with explicit counts and consider human-review capacity when setting alert thresholds.

mistake: High recall does not guarantee that a positive prediction is likely to be a true defect.
takeaway: Use the production base rate and analyze the correct independent unit.

title: Is 85% really better than 82%?
objectives: Separate effect size from uncertainty
Design paired model comparisons
Avoid interpreting p-values as truth probabilities
relevance: A small eval-score increase should not trigger a model migration unless the benefit is credible and useful.

sections.title: The missing information
paragraphs: Model A scores 82% and B scores 85%. The observed difference is three percentage points. Without sample size, dataset composition, pairing, repeated runs, and uncertainty, you cannot judge whether the difference generalizes.

Evaluate both versions on the same held-out cases to reduce noise from case difficulty. Analyze per-case differences. A paired bootstrap resamples case IDs and recomputes the mean difference; keep conversational clusters together.

sections.title: Statistical versus practical significance
paragraphs: A confidence interval expresses uncertainty under a sampling procedure; it is not a probability that this specific fixed parameter lies in the realized interval. A p-value measures how incompatible the observations are with a specified null model, not the chance that the null is true.

Predefine a minimum worthwhile effect and release constraints for latency, cost, safety, and critical slices. A statistically detectable one-point improvement may be worthless if it doubles cost. A non-significant result is not proof of equivalence.

sections.title: Experiment discipline
paragraphs: A false positive (Type I error) rejects a true null. A false negative (Type II error) misses a real effect. Repeatedly checking many prompt variants until one passes increases false-positive risk.

State the hypothesis and stopping rule first. Keep a final untouched evaluation set, report all important slices, and investigate disagreements with human review. Never cherry-pick the most favorable judge configuration.

mistake: A higher point estimate alone does not establish a reliable or useful improvement.
takeaway: Compare paired outcomes, uncertainty, practical effect, and release constraints.

title: Bootstrap evaluation differences
objectives: Resample paired cases with replacement
Compute an interval for score difference
State limitations of your evaluation sample
relevance: Resampling provides an accessible way to quantify uncertainty while preserving per-case model comparisons.

sections.title: The resampling idea
paragraphs: A bootstrap treats your observed independent cases as an empirical population. Sample n case indices with replacement, calculate a statistic, repeat many times, and summarize the resulting distribution.

For paired evaluation, compute B-A for each case before resampling. Do not sample A and B independently when their scores correspond to the same cases. A percentile interval is useful for exploration but can be inaccurate in small or biased samples.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
diff = np.array([0, 1, -1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0], dtype=float)
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
means = [rng.choice(diff, size=len(diff), replace=True).mean()
         for _ in range(2000)]
print(np.percentile(means, [2.5, 97.5]))

sections.title: What an interval cannot fix
paragraphs: Bootstrap does not repair a biased dataset, a miscalibrated judge, or leakage from tuning on evaluation cases. A narrow interval around a biased score is still misleading.

For latency, evaluate comparable workloads and resample independent sessions when requests share a session. For correctness, retain human-adjudicated failures and report uncertainty for critical slices separately.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: Bootstrap intervals depend on the data representing the target population and on the resampling unit. Resampling individual retries from the same incident treats correlated observations as independent and can make intervals too narrow. A grouped bootstrap samples incidents, retaining their associated observations together.

A fixed seed permits a reproducible teaching result but does not establish interval coverage for every distribution or tiny sample. Compare paired candidate-minus-baseline scores within each case before resampling paired differences. Report effect size and interval, not only whether zero is excluded. Test one observation, constant observations and a skewed sample; explain which conclusions remain uncertain when the dataset is small or unrepresentative.

mistake: Resampling individual turns from one conversation breaks the independence assumption.
takeaway: The independent sampling unit determines what confidence means.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A sample estimates a population; uncertainty depends on the sampling process and the independent unit. A 95% confidence procedure covers the fixed parameter in 95% of repeated samples under its assumptions. It does not assign 95% probability to this realized interval.

A hypothesis test compares evidence with a specified null model. Type I error rejects a true null; Type II error misses a real effect. Statistical power depends on effect size, noise, sample size, and the decision threshold.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Pre-register the minimum practical improvement, dataset slices, randomization unit, stopping rule, and safety constraints. Use a paired test when both models answer the same cases; randomize users or sessions for an online A/B test when turns share context.

For a proportion, a Wilson interval is often more stable near zero or one than the normal approximation. For paired differences, resample independent case or conversation IDs. State the method and assumptions with the score.
sections.code:
import math
def wilson(successes,n,z=1.96):
    if n <= 0: raise ValueError("positive sample size required")
    p=successes/n
    center=(p+z*z/(2*n))/(1+z*z/n)
    half=z*math.sqrt(p*(1-p)/n+z*z/(4*n*n))/(1+z*z/n)
    return center-half,center+half
print(wilson(85,100))

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Machine learning estimates a mapping from observed features to a target using examples. Supervised learning has labels; unsupervised learning discovers structure without a predefined target. A classifier chooses a category, a regressor predicts a numeric value, and anomaly detection flags unusual observations without proving a defect.

For CI failures, define PRODUCT_DEFECT, AUTOMATION_DEFECT, ENVIRONMENT, TEST_DATA, and UNKNOWN. Label by evidence available to expert triage, record disagreements, and retain UNKNOWN instead of forcing false certainty. Define the prediction moment before choosing features.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism

Feature extraction turns text and metadata into numbers: TF-IDF for log tokens, numeric duration, and one-hot environment categories. Fit preprocessing only on training examples in a Pipeline. Validate on later incidents or held-out groups to approximate real deployment.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Training fits parameters, validation selects architecture and thresholds, and a final test set estimates the behavior of the selected system. Overfitting captures accidental training patterns; underfitting misses useful structure. Bias is systematic error from restrictions, while variance reflects sensitivity to the sample.

Cross-validation trains and validates repeatedly on different folds. It does not excuse leakage: time order, incident grouping, and transformation fitting still matter. A scaler or vocabulary fitted on all records exposes validation information.

Compare learning curves: a persistent poor fit on both train and validation suggests insufficient representation or excessive regularization; a strong train score and weak validation score suggests overfit, shift, or leakage. Keep the final test set untouched until model selection is complete.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Linear regression fits a numeric target by combining weighted features. Logistic regression applies a sigmoid or multiclass softmax to linear scores to model class probabilities; its name does not mean it predicts a continuous regression target. k-NN votes among nearby observations and depends strongly on representation and scaling.

A decision tree repeatedly partitions features into regions and can express interactions, but a deep tree overfits. Random forests average many randomized trees to reduce variance. Gradient boosting adds learners that correct remaining errors, often requiring careful regularization and validation.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Choose a model based on feature type, dataset size, interpretability, and operational budget. Start with a regularized linear text model; compare tree ensembles on meaningful numeric/categorical features. Use standardized distances for k-NN and evaluate memory and query time because it retains training examples.

Tune depth, regularization, and ensemble size using validation rather than the final test set. For regression report MAE in original units, RMSE to emphasize large mistakes, and R² relative to a mean predictor; R² can be negative.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Accuracy can be high when a rare class is always missed. A confusion matrix counts actual and predicted categories. For a positive class, precision is TP/(TP+FP), recall is TP/(TP+FN), specificity is TN/(TN+FP), and F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.

ROC plots true-positive versus false-positive rates as the threshold varies. PR curves focus on precision/recall and can be more informative when positives are rare. AUC summarizes ranking over thresholds and does not choose your deployed operating point.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Select the threshold on validation data using the cost of misses, false alarms, and human review. Use class weights or sampling carefully and keep evaluation at the natural population prevalence. Calibrate probabilities if decisions require meaningful confidence.

For multiclass triage, compute each class’s metrics and macro averages so frequent environment failures do not hide product-defect errors. A top probability below a validated threshold can route to UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A neuron computes z=w·x+b and applies an activation. Without nonlinear activation, stacking linear layers still produces a linear transformation. Sigmoid maps to (0,1), tanh to (-1,1), ReLU uses max(0,z), and softmax turns a vector of logits into normalized positive probabilities.

A tensor generalizes vectors and matrices to multiple axes. Label batch, feature, and class dimensions: a classification batch shaped (N,D) multiplied by weights (D,C) gives logits (N,C). Shape validity alone does not prove that axes mean the intended things.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Initialize weights with a scale appropriate to the activation rather than all zeros. Use ReLU in a small hidden layer and leave final logits unnormalized when a loss such as CrossEntropyLoss expects logits. Compute stable softmax by subtracting the maximum logit first.
Inspect a single sample before batching. Verify dtype, input shape, class indices, and output dimension. Keep training and evaluation modes explicit when dropout or normalization changes behavior.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Identical zero-initialized hidden weights preserve symmetry and cannot learn distinct features. Applying softmax before a loss that already incorporates log-softmax can weaken or distort optimization. A sigmoid with extreme logits saturates and gives tiny gradients.
Print intermediate shapes and compare a manual forward pass with the framework. Diagnose a wrong tensor axis before changing learning rate or adding layers.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply

A failure classifier is only useful if input features and output class indices remain aligned across training, artifact serialization, and the API. This is a familiar contract-testing problem with numeric tensors.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A derivative measures how a small input change affects a function. A gradient collects derivatives with respect to parameters. Gradient descent updates parameters opposite the gradient to reduce a differentiable loss locally. For L(w)=(w-3)², the derivative is 2(w-3).

Learning rate controls step size. Too small can converge slowly; too large can overshoot or diverge. A lower training loss does not alone establish better generalization. The optimization objective and validation objective may differ.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Compute a forward prediction, scalar loss, gradients, and an update. In PyTorch, zero gradients before the next backward call because gradients accumulate by default. Separate the optimizer step from data iteration and log meaningful loss aggregates.

An epoch is a pass through training data; a minibatch is a subset used for one update. Shuffling improves stochastic training but keep deterministic seeds and independent evaluation splits for reproducibility.
sections.code:
w=0.
for epoch in range(10):
    gradient=2*(w-3)
    w-=.1*gradient
print(w,(w-3)**2)

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Exploding loss can come from excessive learning rate, unscaled features, invalid labels, or an unstable numerical operation. Vanishing gradients can arise through saturated activations or long chains of multiplication.
Test a tiny batch you should be able to overfit. If loss does not decrease there, inspect gradient values, parameter updates, labels, and loss input contract before blaming dataset scale.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
