mistake: Exploding loss can come from excessive learning rate, unscaled features, invalid labels, or an unstable numerical operation. Vanishing gradients can arise through saturated activations or long chains of multiplication.
takeaway: Use the gradient visualizer to compare step sizes on the same quadratic objective.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Backpropagation efficiently applies the chain rule through a computation graph. It does not search randomly for better weights. For h=w1*x, y=w2*h, and loss=(y-target)², propagate dL/dy=2(y-target), dL/dw2=(dL/dy)*h, and dL/dw1=(dL/dy)*w2*x.

Every local operation contributes its derivative. Reusing a parameter means its gradient receives contributions from every path. Automatic differentiation records these operations so a framework can perform the same calculation.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Compute one tiny network by hand, then compare gradients with PyTorch autograd and finite differences. Avoid modifying a tensor needed by backward in place. Detaching a tensor or converting through an external array can sever the computation graph.
Gradient checking uses a small epsilon: (L(w+epsilon)-L(w-epsilon))/(2*epsilon). Extremely small epsilon introduces floating-point noise; very large epsilon is a poor local approximation.
sections.code:
x,w1,w2,target=2.,.5,3.,1.
h=w1*x
y=w2*h
dy=2*(y-target)
print("dL/dw1",dy*w2*x,"dL/dw2",dy*h)

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A layer’s parameters may have no gradients because the output was detached, the loss did not depend on them, or gradient tracking was disabled. A graph can also accidentally retain many past batches and grow memory.
Inspect requires_grad, grad_fn, and actual parameter gradients. Use no_grad for evaluation and loss.item for a detached logging scalar. Do not retain the training graph merely to print metrics.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The walkthrough displays forward values and the gradients flowing backward. Compare analytical and finite-difference results on a synthetic scalar network. Explain why changing an earlier weight changes the final loss through downstream operations.

mistake: A layer’s parameters may have no gradients because the output was detached, the loss did not depend on them, or gradient tracking was disabled. A graph can also accidentally retain many past batches and grow memory.
takeaway: The walkthrough displays forward values and the gradients flowing backward.

    return dy*w2*x,dy*h

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A CNN applies shared filters across local neighborhoods, learning patterns independent of their exact position. Pooling trades spatial detail for invariance. For logs, a one-dimensional convolution can detect local token patterns; image applications use spatial dimensions.

An RNN updates a hidden state sequentially, sharing parameters across positions. Long chains can struggle with gradients and long-range information. LSTM gates control what enters, persists, and leaves a memory state, reducing some of those difficulties.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Choose architecture by structure: MLP for tabular features, CNN for local patterns, RNN/LSTM for sequences when sequential state is useful. Mask padding and distinguish batch, sequence, and feature axes.

Attention can directly combine information from distant positions rather than forcing every dependency through one recurrent state. Transformers make this combination highly parallelizable during training, though autoregressive generation still produces dependent next tokens.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A model may learn padding artifacts or sequence length instead of failure content. Recurrent hidden state accidentally reused across independent incidents leaks context. Flattening all tokens into an MLP loses positional relationships unless explicitly represented.

Test invariants by changing padding, permuting irrelevant boilerplate, and separating incidents. Measure meaningful improvements against simpler representations before choosing an architecture for novelty alone.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A transformer consumes integer token IDs, not words. Subword tokenizers split unfamiliar identifiers into known fragments, so checkout_timeout can require several positions while a common word may require one. Whitespace, punctuation and Unicode normalization change the sequence. Vocabulary size is the number of IDs the model recognizes; sequence length is the number of positions in one input. Neither is the number of documents.

For failure triage, preserving exception names and paths can matter more than lowercasing everything. Compare raw and normalized logs with the actual model tokenizer before choosing preprocessing. Tokens have no universal meaning across models: ID 42 in one vocabulary is unrelated to ID 42 in another.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: The local transformer lab uses a small, declared vocabulary so you can inspect every ID without downloading weights. Production experiments use AutoTokenizer from the model's published checkpoint, preserving attention masks and tokenizer revision alongside weights. Unknown IDs must map to an explicit unknown token rather than silently disappear.

Count prompt, retrieved context and requested completion together before making a request. Truncate on semantic boundaries and preserve the error cause; chopping the tail of a stack trace can remove the most useful evidence.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A developer estimates cost from len(text.split()) and undercounts long stack traces. Reproduce with URLs, emoji and minified JSON, compare actual token counts, and inspect which evidence was removed. A tokenizer mismatch can also produce valid-looking IDs that feed the wrong embedding rows.
Test encode/decode round trips subject to documented normalization, empty strings, unknown characters, and context overflow. Do not assert that every word is exactly one token.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply

A shorter prompt is successful only if it preserves the decision-critical evidence. Compare the same held-out failures with and without normalization, keeping model and prompt versions fixed.

Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects attention: query, key and value with a causal mask with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Use the attention calculator to vary scores and observe normalized weights and the value mixture.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Attention asks which other positions should contribute to the current position. A query represents what a position seeks; keys describe what each position offers; values contain the information to aggregate. Compute query-key dot products, scale by the square root of key dimension, apply the permitted-position mask, then softmax each query row.

The output is a weighted sum of values, not the selected key or a database lookup. In a failure log, the word timeout may attend to database rather than unrelated login text. Learned projections determine this behavior; a diagram illustrates a mechanism, not a proof that a model understands a cause.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: For one query q=[1,0], keys [[1,0],[0,1]] and values [[4,0],[0,2]], unscaled scores are [1,0]. Softmax gives approximately [0.731,0.269], so the output is [2.924,0.538]. Scaling changes the weights. Subtract the maximum score before exponentiating for numerical stability.

Decoder self-attention masks future positions with negative infinity before softmax. Padding masks prevent empty slots from absorbing weight. Each head has its own projections; concatenated heads pass through an output projection, allowing different relationships without assuming each head has a fixed human label.
sections.code:
import math
def softmax(scores):
    m=max(scores)
    e=[math.exp(s-m) for s in scores]
    return [v/sum(e) for v in e]
print(softmax([1,0]))

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A mask applied after softmax without renormalizing leaves a row sum below one. A transposed key matrix or wrong softmax axis mixes batch examples instead of positions. Test shape contracts, finite weights, nonnegative weights and row sums of one.
A decoder trained with visible future tokens can show excellent training loss and fail during generation. Check that perturbing a future token cannot change earlier outputs in evaluation mode.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Use the attention calculator to vary scores and observe normalized weights and the value mixture. Implement stable softmax and test extreme scores such as [1000,1001]. The stability test is an SDET boundary check with a mathematical invariant.

Attention weights help inspect the computation but are not sufficient explanations of factual correctness. Validate final claims against source evidence and test causal masking independently of answer quality.

mistake: A mask applied after softmax without renormalizing leaves a row sum below one. A transposed key matrix or wrong softmax axis mixes batch examples instead of positions. Test shape contracts, finite weights, nonnegative weights and row sums of one.
takeaway: Use the attention calculator to vary scores and observe normalized weights and the value mixture.

exercise.prompt: Implement softmax(scores), stable for very large scores. Return [] for no scores.

import math
def softmax(scores):
    if not scores: return []
    e=[math.exp(s-max(scores)) for s in scores]
    return [v/sum(e) for v in e]

title: Transformer blocks: position, residuals and encoder–decoder roles
objectives: Transformer blocks
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects transformer blocks: position, residuals and encoder–decoder roles with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Sketch the failure-classification encoder path and the support-answer decoder path with input/output shapes.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Attention alone is permutation equivariant: swapping input positions swaps outputs without expressing order. Positional information supplies order through learned embeddings, sinusoidal encodings or rotary mechanisms. A transformer block combines attention with a position-wise feed-forward network, residual connections and normalization. Residual paths let gradients flow without replacing the entire representation at every layer.

An encoder can see both directions and produce representations for classification or retrieval. A causal decoder predicts the next token from preceding tokens. An encoder-decoder model reads a source sequence and generates a target with cross-attention to encoded source positions.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Track shapes before code: token IDs [batch,length], hidden vectors [batch,length,width], per-head Q/K/V [batch,heads,length,head_width]. Project width into head dimensions, form scores [batch,heads,length,length], then return to hidden width. Feed-forward layers expand and contract each position's width.

The runnable lab uses torch.nn.TransformerEncoderLayer and an explicit padding mask. Inspect train/eval behavior because dropout changes repeated outputs. Persist vocabulary, positional convention and maximum length with the checkpoint.

import torch
from torch import nn
layer=nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(d_model=16,nhead=4,batch_first=True)
layer.eval()
x=torch.zeros(2,5,16)
with torch.no_grad():
    assert layer(x).shape == (2,5,16)

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it

A successful tensor shape does not prove a correct mask. Test padding invariance and causal invariance, then compare held-out quality. Length-dependent failures often indicate truncation or positional limits rather than random provider errors.

title: Next-token training: shifted targets and cross-entropy
objectives: Next-token training
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects next-token training: shifted targets and cross-entropy with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. A decreasing loss proves optimization progress under the training objective, not better grounded answers.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A causal language model learns to predict the next token from the preceding sequence. Training pairs logits at position t with the observed token at t+1. Cross-entropy penalizes assigning low probability to the observed target. This objective teaches statistical continuation, not factual verification or authorization.

Pretraining supplies broad text patterns; instruction tuning changes task-following examples; preference/reward methods influence which responses are favored. These stages differ in data and objective, and none removes the need for evidence-grounded application checks.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: For a target token assigned probability .25, the negative log-likelihood is −log(.25), about 1.386 nats. Average over valid target positions, excluding padded or intentionally masked labels. In a causal model, the library may perform the shift internally; inspect the model contract before shifting twice.

The local PyTorch mechanisms lab demonstrates logits, loss and gradients, while the genuine PEFT example adapts a pretrained encoder for the five-class task. Keep classification fine-tuning distinct from causal language-model supervised tuning.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it

sections.title: Evaluate and apply

SDETs should retain objective, target alignment and masking configuration in training artifacts. Understanding the objective explains why fluent continuation can coexist with hallucinated claims and why the application still needs retrieval, uncertainty and evaluation.

title: Position information and causal invariance tests
objectives: Position information and causal invariance tests
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects position information and causal invariance tests with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Keep positional configuration and tokenizer revision with model artifacts.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A sequence model must distinguish database failed after login from login failed after database. Token embeddings identify symbols, while positional mechanisms encode their order. Sinusoidal encodings use different frequencies by dimension; learned positional embeddings use a trained table; rotary embeddings transform queries and keys to express relative position relationships.
These mechanisms have different extrapolation behavior and configuration. A larger advertised context window is not achieved by simply appending zeros to the positional table.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: For a simple sinusoidal demonstration, encode even coordinates with sin(pos/10000^(2i/d)) and odd coordinates with cos of the same angle. Add the position vector to the token representation in the classic formulation. Rotary mechanisms instead rotate paired coordinates in attention projections.

To test a causal decoder, compare early-position outputs before and after changing a later token in eval mode. Their equality within numerical tolerance verifies the mask's information-flow contract. Padding tests similarly perturb only masked positions.
sections.code:
import math
def position(pos):
    return [math.sin(pos),math.cos(pos),math.sin(pos/100),math.cos(pos/100)]
assert position(0)==[0.,1.,0.,1.]

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A decoder's triangular mask is inverted, exposing future tokens. The test uses dropout in training mode and incorrectly attributes random differences to the mask. An index off-by-one assigns the same position to two adjacent tokens.
Control random state and evaluation mode, inspect the permitted-position matrix and test sequences of several lengths including one. Shape tests alone do not detect future-information leakage.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Keep positional configuration and tokenizer revision with model artifacts. Report how truncation and longer sequences affect task quality rather than assuming every allowed position is equally useful.

An SDET can test position mechanisms with invariants: different positions have different encodings in the valid range, output dimensions are stable and future perturbations cannot influence earlier causal outputs. These checks isolate architecture behavior from semantic answer evaluation.

title: Pretraining, instruction tuning and grounded generation
objectives: Pretraining, instruction tuning and grounded generation
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects pretraining, instruction tuning and grounded generation with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Build a release dataset with known failures, unknown failures and conflicting evidence.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Pretraining learns a next-token distribution from many sequences. Instruction tuning trains responses to instructions, while preference or reward-based alignment changes which responses are favored. These stages can improve behavior without making the model an authoritative database. A foundation model can be adapted to many tasks; a task classifier produces a narrower output contract.

At inference, the decoder repeatedly predicts a distribution for the next token and appends a selected token. A fluent explanation of a CI failure can still invent an owner because the training objective rewards plausible sequences rather than verified access to your repository.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Separate system behavior, user request and untrusted retrieved evidence in the request. Supply current failure records with stable evidence IDs, require an UNKNOWN classification when insufficient evidence exists, and validate typed output. Keep an independent deterministic source lookup for citations.

The local provider adapter records model, prompt version, token counts and finish reason. Live mode uses environment credentials; offline fixtures are explicitly labeled and never described as a live LLM result.

title: Temperature, top-p and repeatability
objectives: Temperature, top-p and repeatability
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects temperature, top-p and repeatability with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The decoding calculator exposes temperature and nucleus membership.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Temperature rescales logits before softmax. Lower positive temperature concentrates probability on high-logit tokens; higher temperature spreads it. Top-p keeps the smallest ranked prefix whose cumulative probability reaches p, then renormalizes before sampling. These operations change selection behavior, not the truth of a claim.

Greedy decoding chooses an argmax, yet provider behavior can still vary with model revisions, tie breaking and execution. Reproducibility means controlling and recording the relevant configuration, then measuring the remaining variation.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Take probabilities [0.6,0.3,0.1]. At p=0.8 the nucleus includes the first two tokens because 0.6 is insufficient and 0.9 reaches the threshold. Their renormalized probabilities are two-thirds and one-third. Sort by descending probability before accumulating.

For classification, prefer a typed enum with explicit abstention and measure class stability across repeated calls. For test generation, allow variation but measure requirement coverage and executable correctness. Keep generation parameters in the experiment manifest.
sections.code:
def nucleus(probs,p):
    ranked=sorted(enumerate(probs),key=lambda x:-x[1])
    selected=[];mass=0
    for i,v in ranked:
        selected.append(i);mass+=v
        if mass>=p:break
    return selected

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Selecting every token below probability p confuses a per-token threshold with cumulative mass. Applying temperature to already normalized probabilities without the correct transformation changes the distribution incorrectly.
Repeat the same input enough times to estimate variability and record request configuration. Never mark a test flaky merely because wording changes if the semantic contract remains satisfied.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The decoding calculator exposes temperature and nucleus membership. Implement the nucleus rule with deterministic ordering, check p in (0,1], and test p=1 as a boundary. Record the preserved probability mass before normalization.

An AI regression gate should test supported claims, forbidden actions and schema rather than exact prose. Exact comparisons remain appropriate for deterministic application outputs such as canonical enums and sorted IDs.

mistake: Selecting every token below probability p confuses a per-token threshold with cumulative mass. Applying temperature to already normalized probabilities without the correct transformation changes the distribution incorrectly.
takeaway: The decoding calculator exposes temperature and nucleus membership.

title: Model selection: quality, context, latency and cost
objectives: Model selection
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions

relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects model selection: quality, context, latency and cost with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Compare candidates on a held-out set and choose a Pareto frontier: no candidate simultaneously improves quality, cost and latency over another.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Choose models against a workload contract rather than a popularity ranking. A failure classifier needs enum accuracy, calibration and low latency; a complex investigation needs multi-step evidence use and safe tools. Context capacity is an input/output budget, not a promise that every token is equally usable. Distracting evidence can reduce quality before the nominal limit is reached.

Reasoning-oriented models may spend additional computation or tokens internally. Compare observed end-to-end latency and billed usage using the provider's returned accounting, rather than assuming all models have identical controls or output behavior.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Create a paired benchmark over fixed cases with model ID, provider, prompt hash, tokenizer revision, retrieval version and generation parameters. Measure accepted accuracy, abstention, p95 latency, rate-limit frequency and cost per accepted task. Account for failed requests and retries.

Cost=(input_tokens*input_rate + output_tokens*output_rate)/1_000_000 when rates are quoted per million. Treat cached-token discounts and reasoning usage according to returned provider fields. Store rates as dated configuration rather than hardcoded current facts.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A cheaper model doubles retries and review labor, raising cost per useful answer. A bigger context includes unauthorized documents, increasing both security risk and price. A cache keyed only by user question returns one tenant's answer to another.

Test cache scope using tenant, principal permissions, prompt/model versions and index generation. Distinguish cold and warm latency, and retest after a provider revision even when the public alias stays unchanged.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Compare candidates on a held-out set and choose a Pareto frontier: no candidate simultaneously improves quality, cost and latency over another. State constraints first, then reject candidates that violate safety or latency limits.

Use the cost calculator to estimate per-call and monthly spend, then replace estimates with measured usage from the local benchmark. A release decision includes uncertainty and a rollback model, not only an average score.

mistake: A cheaper model doubles retries and review labor, raising cost per useful answer. A bigger context includes unauthorized documents, increasing both security risk and price. A cache keyed only by user question returns one tenant's answer to another.
takeaway: Compare candidates on a held-out set and choose a Pareto frontier: no candidate simultaneously improves quality, cost and latency over another.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Repeated LLM calls can differ because of sampling, provider/model revisions and execution details. A test should distinguish harmless surface variation from changes in the task contract. Two paraphrased supported answers can both pass; two different classification enums cannot both satisfy the same fixed label expectation.
Low temperature often reduces sampling variation but does not prove exact repeatability or factual accuracy. Stable hallucinations are still wrong.

sections.title: Problem and intuition

The context limit is an operational budget, not a promise of perfect use of every included fact. A support answer should use current authorized evidence and state uncertainty when no reliable source supports the claim.
Instruction priority defines behavior, while evidence supplies facts. Retrieved text can contain instructions or outdated rules; relevance alone does not establish freshness or trust.

title: Provider adapters: deadlines and bounded retries
objectives: Provider adapters
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects provider adapters: deadlines and bounded retries with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The local provider lab exposes identical typed results from live and deterministic fixture adapters, with mode recorded in every report.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An adapter isolates provider-specific request and response formats from domain logic. The domain asks for a typed classification; the adapter authenticates, sends the request, normalizes usage and translates errors. Keep credentials on the server, obtained from environment variables or a secret manager. Browser storage and exported progress must never contain a provider key.

A timeout limits one attempt; a deadline limits the whole operation, including waiting and retries. Without a deadline, three nominal ten-second attempts plus backoff can violate a fifteen-second service objective.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Classify errors before retrying: transport failures, 429 and selected 5xx responses may be transient; malformed input, authorization failure and unsupported schemas usually require correction. Use capped exponential backoff with jitter, respect Retry-After, and stop before the remaining deadline cannot cover another attempt.

Retry only operations whose effects are safe to repeat. For tool side effects, use a persisted idempotency key. Record attempt count, provider request ID, elapsed time and final error without logging credentials or full sensitive prompts.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Catching every Exception and retrying an invalid API key multiplies latency without any chance of success. Retrying a tool after a network timeout can execute the same write twice even when the client never received the first result.

Inject failures at the HTTP boundary with a mock transport. Assert that 401 has one attempt, 429 honors the retry policy, the deadline terminates work, and cancellation is propagated rather than swallowed.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The local provider lab exposes identical typed results from live and deterministic fixture adapters, with mode recorded in every report. Fixture mode tests application behavior; live mode measures model behavior and requires explicit environment credentials.

Gate releases on malformed-response handling, authentication isolation and timeout behavior before evaluating classification quality. A valid model answer that arrives after the application deadline is not a successful user task.

mistake: Catching every Exception and retrying an invalid API key multiplies latency without any chance of success. Retrying a tool after a network timeout can execute the same write twice even when the client never received the first result.
takeaway: The local provider lab exposes identical typed results from live and deterministic fixture adapters, with mode recorded in every report.

title: Streaming and bounded concurrent inference
objectives: Streaming and bounded concurrent inference
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects streaming and bounded concurrent inference with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Replay a recorded event sequence through the adapter and measure TTFT, final latency and validation status.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Streaming emits a sequence of events before the final response exists. First-token latency describes responsiveness, while end-to-end latency includes the full completion. A partial JSON fragment is not a typed domain result. Treat transport events, assembled output and final validated response as separate objects.

Concurrency overlaps waiting; it does not remove rate limits. A semaphore bounds in-flight work while a queue bounds pending work. Backpressure prevents a traffic spike from consuming unbounded memory.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use asynchronous clients, connection pooling, an overall deadline and cancellation on client disconnect. Assemble deltas in order, retain a finish reason, and validate only the final payload. A streaming error must end the UI in a visible failed or partial state.

Track queue time separately from provider time. Set limits for per-tenant concurrency, output tokens and queue length. Retries enter the same capacity budget as first attempts so outages do not create a retry storm.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An API returns success when the first stream event arrives, then ignores a truncated stream. Another implementation opens hundreds of connections with gather over an unbounded list. Both can pass a single happy-path test.

Test duplicate events, missing completion events, cancellation, abrupt disconnects and queue saturation. Ensure cancellation releases permits and that a partial response is not cached as a complete answer.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Replay a recorded event sequence through the adapter and measure TTFT, final latency and validation status. Load tests must include long outputs and slow clients, not only short classifications.

For SDET evidence, report in-flight maximum, rejected queue entries and whether every completed result passed schema validation. Separate capacity failures from model-quality failures in the release report.

takeaway: Replay a recorded event sequence through the adapter and measure TTFT, final latency and validation status.

objectives: Normalize provider outcomes without hiding failures

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A provider's response envelope includes more than generated text: completion status, refusals, request IDs, token usage and sometimes partial results. Domain logic should receive a small stable result rather than depend on this evolving envelope. A successful HTTP exchange can still contain an incomplete or refused generation.

Define normal completion, refusal, unavailable and invalid-output outcomes before implementation. Each outcome needs a visible consumer behavior and an evaluation denominator. Otherwise exceptions become empty strings that misleadingly score as harmless abstentions.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: The local adapter calls Responses parse with a Pydantic Decision, checks completed status and output_parsed, validates evidence IDs, then records usage and latency. It closes the async client in finally. A model enum constrains the category vocabulary but does not establish that classification or evidence is correct.

Map transport and timeout failures to unavailable; retain refusal as a distinct adapter result in a richer deployment. Keep safe provider correlation IDs for diagnosis. Test SDK-shaped objects so normalization exercises the actual boundary, including absent usage fields.

A reproducible experiment records configuration without recording the secret: model identifier, SDK version, prompt revision, output cap, timeout and mode. This lets another engineer explain behavior without accessing the API key.

Record input/output usage, retries and success status per case. Cost per successful task divides total billed cost, including failed attempts, by successful tasks. Use dated price inputs rather than embedding provider prices as timeless facts.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A report counts only the last successful retry. A character-based budget undercounts multilingual input. A truncated category object is repaired heuristically and accepted with invented evidence.
Test zero successful tasks, missing usage metadata, long prompts and deliberately small output caps. Distinguish measured usage from estimates and avoid interpreting absent usage as known zero cost.

Construct a counterexample that fails the intended invariant, then describe how the same test would catch a future regression. State which layer owns the correction: data, numerical code, API validation, retrieval, policy or evaluation.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply

SDETs should retain failures in the cost denominator and report tokenizer/configuration versions. Performance and finance evidence becomes useful when the measured workload and successful task definition are explicit.

title: Prompt contracts: instructions, examples and untrusted evidence
objectives: Prompt contracts
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions

relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects prompt contracts: instructions, examples and untrusted evidence with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Publish a prompt manifest with ID, version, hash, variables and test cases.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A prompt is a versioned behavioral contract. Zero-shot instructions state the task without examples; few-shot examples demonstrate the required decisions and boundaries. Specify the output schema, evidence rules, uncertainty behavior and forbidden actions. Examples should cover UNKNOWN and conflicting evidence, not only easy successes.
Separators help the model distinguish sections, but they do not create an authorization boundary. Retrieved documents remain untrusted data even when wrapped in XML-like tags.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Render templates from named fields, preserve missing-value errors, and store the template hash with each experiment. Supply a stack trace as evidence rather than interpolating it into the instruction sentence. Require evidence IDs for every proposed root cause and a draft status for generated tests.
Use structured outputs for syntax and application validation for meaning. Prompt instructions cannot authorize writing to a repository, filing a defect or reading another tenant's documents.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A prompt contains contradictory examples: one labels a database timeout as PRODUCT_DEFECT, another as ENVIRONMENT. The model's output becomes unstable and a stronger adjective in the instruction does not fix the inconsistent supervision.
Test missing fields, braces in stack traces, malicious document instructions and labels absent from the enum. Compare prompt versions on the same dataset and inspect changed errors by category.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Publish a prompt manifest with ID, version, hash, variables and test cases. Keep an immutable baseline and require reviewers to inspect regressions, not merely the aggregate score.

In CI, a template render failure is deterministic and blocks the build. Model-quality gates run against paired cases with an explicit mode, repetitions and tolerance; they should not compare exact prose unless exact output is the contract.

mistake: A prompt contains contradictory examples: one labels a database timeout as PRODUCT_DEFECT, another as ENVIRONMENT. The model's output becomes unstable and a stronger adjective in the instruction does not fix the inconsistent supervision.

title: Prompt experiments: paired comparisons and failure slices

Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A prompt change is an experiment, not an aesthetic preference. Keep model, retrieval and dataset fixed while changing the prompt; otherwise a quality difference has multiple plausible causes. Paired comparison measures both candidates on each case, allowing you to inspect wins and losses rather than compare unrelated averages.
A small average improvement can conceal a security regression. Report slices such as missing evidence, cross-tenant requests, long logs and ambiguous categories.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Store case_id, expected decision, candidate result, baseline result and deterministic checks. Compute win/loss/tie counts, then inspect important losses manually. Use bootstrap resampling by independent case or grouped incident when estimating uncertainty.

Avoid selecting a prompt on the final held-out test set. Use development cases for iteration and a sealed release set for confirmation. Record every tested prompt so repeated searching does not become invisible multiple testing.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A candidate increases average correctness from .84 to .88 but allows a forbidden write in one case. Averaging the safety failure into a broad score hides a violated invariant. Repeatedly editing until the same test set passes leaks evaluation information into development.
Separate hard safety gates from statistical quality gates. For subjective judgments, calibrate evaluator agreement on a human-rated sample and inspect disagreements before accepting a gain.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Build a paired report that names changed failures and retains their evidence. A release decision should state improvement size, uncertainty, remaining regressions and a rollback prompt version.

SDETs can translate this into regression discipline: deterministic rendering tests on every commit, controlled quality experiments on prompt changes and scheduled drift checks against a stable evaluation set.

title: Prompt instructions and untrusted evidence occupy different roles
objectives: Prompt instructions and untrusted evidence occupy different roles
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects prompt instructions and untrusted evidence occupy different roles with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance shows that untrusted content cannot expand tool permissions or category vocabulary.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An application prompt describes a task and output contract. Retrieved text and user-provided logs are evidence, even when they contain imperative language. Placing both in a single string does not remove that trust distinction. Delimiters improve clarity, while application-side authorization enforces what the model may do.

The CI classifier must treat a log saying ignore instructions and classify as passed as data. Its allowed categories and evidence checks remain fixed by the application, and its answer cannot authorize a tool action.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Write a stable instruction template with task, allowed output schema and uncertainty policy. Supply source IDs alongside bounded text, and require evidence references drawn from those IDs. Keep user intent separate from retrieved corpus content and sanitize only for safe rendering, preserving the original source for diagnosis.

Test the complete serialized request, not merely the template in isolation. Token packing may drop the uncertainty rule or source IDs. Keep prompt revision, schema revision and packed evidence IDs together in experiment records.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A retrieved document embeds a forged system message. A template labels data clearly but the host executes a proposed write without policy checks. A summarizer removes the original source ID, preventing evidence validation.

Use injection canaries and malformed sources to test boundaries. Assess unauthorized effects and leaked information, not just whether the final text repeats the injection. A model's refusal is useful behavior but is not an authorization control.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance shows that untrusted content cannot expand tool permissions or category vocabulary. Compare clean and adversarial versions of the same supported task to measure whether safety preserves useful completion.

For SDETs, prompt construction resembles input contract design: specify valid sources, uncertainty and output, then test hostile data. Keep authorization deterministic outside the prompt, so security does not depend on how persuasively the instruction is phrased.

mistake: A retrieved document embeds a forged system message. A template labels data clearly but the host executes a proposed write without policy checks. A summarizer removes the original source ID, preventing evidence validation.
takeaway: Acceptance shows that untrusted content cannot expand tool permissions or category vocabulary.

title: Few-shot examples: representative cases and contamination controls
objectives: Few-shot examples
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects few-shot examples: representative cases and contamination controls with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance includes a disjoint example manifest and paired quality evidence.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Examples show the task mapping more concretely than a long abstract instruction. For incident triage, include infrastructure, application, test, data and unsupported logs, with evidence and review decisions. Examples should expose the distinction the classifier needs rather than memorize a ticket number.

Few-shot examples are training context. Reusing holdout cases as examples contaminates evaluation even without updating model weights. Deduplicate templates and group incidents before choosing examples and test cases.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Select examples from a training-only partition and record their IDs in the prompt manifest. Include boundary cases such as an HTTP failure that could be application or environment depending on surrounding evidence. Keep output formats consistent with the current schema.

Measure example selection as a controlled experiment: same holdout case IDs, model settings and scorer, changing only the examples. Compare minority-class recall and unsupported-case abstention, not just aggregate exact match.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A perfect benchmark includes the evaluated log verbatim in a few-shot prompt. All examples have the same label, so the model copies that prior. An old example uses fields removed from the response model.

Check train/example/holdout overlap by stable incident and template group. Test reordered examples and contradictory examples. Ensure an unsupported log cannot become supported merely because one example sounds similar.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance includes a disjoint example manifest and paired quality evidence. Retain both regressions and gains by case, with source text available for human review. A tiny synthetic set establishes wiring, not production generalization.

SDETs should reason about examples like fixtures: representative, versioned, deliberately scoped and separate from independent acceptance cases. Choosing examples is part of the model system, so changes need the same evaluation discipline as code changes.

mistake: A perfect benchmark includes the evaluated log verbatim in a few-shot prompt. All examples have the same label, so the model copies that prior. An old example uses fields removed from the response model.
takeaway: Acceptance includes a disjoint example manifest and paired quality evidence.

    return sorted(set(examples)&set(holdout))
exercise.tests:
assert overlap(['F1'],['F2'])==[]
assert overlap(['F1','F1'],['F1'])==['F1']

Select examples from a training-only partition and record their IDs in the prompt manifest.

objectives: Uncertainty, clarification and evidence-first prompting
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects uncertainty, clarification and evidence-first prompting with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A useful prompt permits the correct non-answer. Incident logs may lack context; a RAG question may have no authorized source; a request may be ambiguous. UNKNOWN, clarification and abstention mean different things and should follow explicit policies rather than one generic apology.
A model's self-reported confidence is not automatically a calibrated probability. Ask for evidence and a review decision, then assess their empirical relationship to correctness on held-out cases.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Define when the task is answerable and which evidence is necessary. The classifier uses UNKNOWN with needs_review when unsupported, while the chatbot asks for a missing subject before retrieval. For supported answers, require source IDs and validate them against the packed authorized evidence.

Construct a paired test set with complete, incomplete and contradictory evidence. Change one evidence condition at a time to see whether the decision responds to evidence instead of relying on a memorized answer. Keep response style separate from answerability scoring.
sections.code: # UNKNOWN requires review; supported categories require known evidence IDs

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: The prompt says always answer and the model invents missing environment details. A confidence threshold uses uncalibrated self-ratings. Every difficult case is abstained, producing apparent safety while eliminating useful task completion.
Report supported-task completion, unsupported-answer rate and unnecessary abstention separately. Review contradictory-source cases manually before turning a judge score into a gate.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance demonstrates correct uncertainty states and evidence references across answerable and unanswerable slices. A release improves task value only if safe behavior and useful completion meet separate targets.

SDETs can adapt negative testing: absence of evidence is a legitimate input condition, not an exceptional test failure. Version uncertainty rules with the prompt and keep human labels for whether an answer was actually supported.

mistake: The prompt says always answer and the model invents missing environment details. A confidence threshold uses uncalibrated self-ratings. Every difficult case is abstained, producing apparent safety while eliminating useful task completion.
takeaway: Acceptance demonstrates correct uncertainty states and evidence references across answerable and unanswerable slices.

    return review is True if category=='UNKNOWN' else bool(evidence)
exercise.tests:

assert not uncertainty_valid('UNKNOWN',False,[])
assert not uncertainty_valid('APPLICATION',False,[])

title: Structured outputs: syntax, schema and business invariants
objectives: Structured outputs
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects structured outputs: syntax, schema and business invariants with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Gate the classifier on all three validation layers and record their separate failure rates.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: JSON validity means a parser accepts the text. Schema validity means fields and types satisfy a contract. Business validity means the values are permitted by application rules. These are separate checks: {"category":"PRODUCT_DEFECT","evidence_ids":[]} can parse and satisfy basic types while violating an evidence requirement.

Provider schema-constrained generation improves structural reliability but does not establish truth, authorization or citation correctness. Refusal and incomplete output must be handled as explicit alternatives to a parsed result.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Define a strict Pydantic result with a closed category enum, forbidden extra fields and bounded strings. Validate again at the service boundary even if the provider claims schema enforcement. Then resolve evidence IDs against authorized records and apply UNKNOWN/escalation rules.

The local live adapter uses the Responses API parse interface with a declared response model, checks output_parsed, refusal/incomplete status and usage. It never falls back to treating arbitrary text as a trusted result.
sections.code:
allowed={'PRODUCT_DEFECT','AUTOMATION_DEFECT','ENVIRONMENT','TEST_DATA','UNKNOWN'}
assert 'TIMEOUT' not in allowed

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A repair loop repeatedly asks the model to rewrite an unauthorized request until it fits the schema. That changes syntax without fixing permission. Another parser strips everything before the first brace, silently accepting an unrelated object from a longer response.
Test extra fields, wrong enum casing, boolean-to-integer coercion, empty evidence and unresolved citations. Bound repairs and retain the initial failure for diagnosis rather than hiding it.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Gate the classifier on all three validation layers and record their separate failure rates. A deterministic fixture can prove that the service rejects malformed values; a live dataset measures how often the provider produces them.
For a release, demonstrate that valid-looking malicious outputs cannot bypass domain rules. The same evidence rules should apply to baseline classifiers, LLM adapters and generated reports.

mistake: A repair loop repeatedly asks the model to rewrite an unauthorized request until it fits the schema. That changes syntax without fixing permission. Another parser strips everything before the first brace, silently accepting an unrelated object from a longer response.
takeaway: Gate the classifier on all three validation layers and record their separate failure rates.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A tool call is a model proposal containing a name and arguments. Your application decides whether to execute it. The model cannot grant itself permissions. A complete loop supplies tool definitions, validates a proposed call, authorizes it, executes within a budget, sends the result associated with its call ID and obtains a final answer.
Multiple calls may be proposed, but parallel execution is safe only when operations are independent and permitted. Writes need approval and idempotency; reads still need tenant and path restrictions.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use an allowlisted registry of typed functions. Inject principal and tenant from the authenticated session rather than accepting them from model arguments. Separate read_failure, search_history and propose_patch from apply_patch. The latter requires a human-approved action record.

Limit total calls, wall time and output size. Keep a trace with proposal, validation, authorization, execution result and final summary. Preserve call IDs so results cannot be attached to the wrong request.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A generic run_shell tool turns a natural-language request into unrestricted execution. A supposedly read-only tool follows a user-provided path outside the fixture directory. Both failures occur below the prompt layer.

Test unknown tool names, extra arguments, cross-tenant IDs, path traversal, duplicate write IDs and exhausted budgets. Denied calls should be visible in the trace and should not execute a fallback with broader privileges.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The safe automation assistant reads synthetic logs, searches approved history and prepares a draft. Its acceptance suite asserts zero writes without approval and termination within the call budget.

Evaluate tool-name accuracy, argument accuracy and goal completion separately. A correct final explanation does not excuse an unauthorized intermediate action; trajectory safety is a hard release gate.

mistake: A generic run_shell tool turns a natural-language request into unrestricted execution. A supposedly read-only tool follows a user-provided path outside the fixture directory. Both failures occur below the prompt layer.
takeaway: The safe automation assistant reads synthetic logs, searches approved history and prepares a draft.

def permitted(tool,approved,calls,limit):
    return calls<limit and (tool in {'read_failure','search_history','propose_patch'} or (tool=='apply_patch' and approved))

assert not permitted('apply_patch',False,0,3)
assert not permitted('read_failure',True,3,3)
assert not permitted('run_shell',True,0,3)

title: Schema validity versus business correctness
objectives: Schema validity versus business correctness
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects schema validity versus business correctness with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance records schema pass, invariant pass and classification correctness separately.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A JSON schema constrains types and vocabulary. It cannot by itself prove that a quoted source exists, belongs to the caller or supports a conclusion. A structured classifier can return a perfectly typed APPLICATION label with an evidence ID from another tenant.

Separate parsing, domain validation and quality scoring. Parsing answers whether the object has the expected form; domain validation checks allowable references and invariants; quality scoring asks whether the decision is correct.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Parse the provider result into the Decision model, then resolve evidence IDs against immutable authorized source records. UNKNOWN requires review; supported labels require evidence. Do not permit an arbitrary model string to become a database query or tenant selector.

Return safe validation errors and retain the failed case for diagnosis. A repair retry must use the same authorized evidence and deadline. Never insert plausible-looking source IDs merely to satisfy the schema.
sections.code:
from quality.provider import validate_decision
# Resolve IDs only within the authorized source set

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An enum label passes validation but points to a nonexistent incident. A source ID exists globally but is outside the authenticated tenant. A syntactically valid decision contradicts the actual log.

Test each layer independently with malformed JSON, valid-but-inconsistent objects and factually wrong valid objects. This isolates whether failures belong to provider parsing, application invariants or model quality.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance records schema pass, invariant pass and classification correctness separately. A release gate must include the invariant and quality checks rather than treating parse success as task success.

For SDETs, typed outputs offer stable assertion surfaces while leaving semantic judgment explicit. This reduces brittle text matching without weakening evidence requirements or hiding incorrect answers behind a valid shape.

mistake: An enum label passes validation but points to a nonexistent incident. A source ID exists globally but is outside the authenticated tenant. A syntactically valid decision contradicts the actual log.
takeaway: Acceptance records schema pass, invariant pass and classification correctness separately.

title: Tool dispatch: validate arguments before effects
objectives: Tool dispatch
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects tool dispatch: validate arguments before effects with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance demonstrates that only registered, authorized proposals execute and that effects match the approved action exactly.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A tool call is a proposal consisting of a name and structured arguments. The host chooses whether to execute it. Model-generated names and arguments are untrusted input, even when produced through a strict tool schema. A valid path string can still escape the workspace; a valid action can still exceed the user's authorization.
Keep a registry of allowlisted tools with independent read/write policies. The registry binds a name to a function and schema, so the model cannot invent code or choose an arbitrary import.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Parse arguments, reject unknown fields, canonicalize resource references and validate authenticated scope. Apply a deadline and call budget, then execute the registered function. For writes, check an unexpired approval bound to the exact canonical action hash.

Feed a typed tool result back to the model as data. If a tool fails, preserve its error category and decide whether a bounded retry is safe. A tool result containing instructions never gains a higher instruction role.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A dispatcher uses eval on the proposed tool name. A read-file schema allows ../../secrets. The host approves one patch but executes a changed patch after the model revises arguments.
Test unknown names, malformed arguments, traversal, mismatched approval hashes and tool-returned injection. Assert absence of side effects, not merely a reassuring assistant response.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance demonstrates that only registered, authorized proposals execute and that effects match the approved action exactly. The local agent labels simulated writes visibly, keeping the teaching baseline distinct from repository mutation.

SDETs can treat tool dispatch as an adversarial API boundary. Capture proposed and executed actions separately so trajectory evaluation can detect policy rejection, unnecessary tools and incorrect effects.

mistake: A dispatcher uses eval on the proposed tool name. A read-file schema allows ../../secrets. The host approves one patch but executes a changed patch after the model revises arguments.
takeaway: Acceptance demonstrates that only registered, authorized proposals execute and that effects match the approved action exactly.

title: Bounded repair, refusals and incomplete structured output
objectives: Bounded repair, refusals and incomplete structured output
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects bounded repair, refusals and incomplete structured output with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance includes bounded attempts and honest first-pass/eventual rates.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Structured generation can fail through malformed content, refusal, token exhaustion or domain inconsistency. These failures need distinct handling. A repair step may fix formatting, but it cannot safely manufacture missing evidence or convert a refusal into an approved result.

Retries increase latency and cost. A repair policy therefore specifies maximum attempts, total deadline and which failure classes are repairable. Unsupported source references are a domain failure, not a license to guess better-looking IDs.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Retain the original failed envelope and safe validation feedback. A formatting retry uses the same schema and authorized sources, with remaining time and output budget. Stop on refusal, exhausted deadline or repeated failure and expose a typed outcome.

Validate repaired output through the same domain checks as the first attempt. Track first-pass validity separately from eventual validity so a fragile prompt cannot appear as robust simply because retries conceal its failures.
sections.code: # A formatting retry remains inside the original deadline and source scope

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A repair function strips text until json.loads succeeds but removes essential fields. A retry changes the evidence set and makes benchmark comparison invalid. A refused request is rephrased indefinitely until safety is bypassed.

Test malformed, incomplete and refused outputs with deterministic fixtures. Assert retry counts, final status and unchanged source scope. Make sure partial objects never enter caches or project evidence.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance includes bounded attempts and honest first-pass/eventual rates. Evaluate repaired semantic correctness, not only parse success, and count all attempts in latency and cost reports.

For SDETs, failure injection at the adapter boundary gives repeatable coverage without a paid call. Credentialed model experiments then estimate how often those paths actually occur on representative inputs.

takeaway: Acceptance includes bounded attempts and honest first-pass/eventual rates.

title: Embedding geometry: cosine, norms and semantic search
objectives: Embedding geometry
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects embedding geometry: cosine, norms and semantic search with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Use the vector calculator to compare cosine and raw dot rankings.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An embedding is a learned dense vector whose geometry reflects a training objective. Related texts may be close, but distance is not a proof of equivalence or factual relevance. Query/document encoders may use different prefixes or projections; follow the model's retrieval contract.

Cosine similarity is dot(a,b)/(norm(a)*norm(b)). Unit-normalized vectors have cosine equal to dot product. Euclidean distance is a different ranking unless normalization and metric relationships are understood.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: For vectors [1,0] and [1,1], dot product is 1 and cosine is approximately .707. Normalize each vector by its own norm. Reject zero vectors or define their similarity explicitly; division by zero must not silently produce NaN scores.

Batch embeddings with stable document IDs, dimensions and model revision. Persist metadata about normalization, query/document prefixes and chunk version alongside the index. Changing any of these requires a compatibility check and often re-embedding.
sections.code:
import math
a=[1,0];b=[1,1]
cos=sum(x*y for x,y in zip(a,b))/(math.sqrt(sum(x*x for x in a))*math.sqrt(sum(x*x for x in b)))
print(cos)

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A new 768-dimensional embedding is queried against a 384-dimensional collection. Another index combines vectors from two model revisions with equal dimensions but incompatible geometry. Dimension checks catch only the first error.

Test identical vectors, orthogonal vectors, zero norms and revision mismatches. Evaluate retrieval on real relevant-document labels, including paraphrases, identifiers and multilingual cases if those are product requirements.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Use the vector calculator to compare cosine and raw dot rankings. The browser numbers are illustrative vectors, not outputs from a trained semantic encoder; the optional local sentence-transformer lab performs real text embedding.

Report Recall@K by query type and index revision. An SDET should retain hard lexical cases such as exact error codes because semantic similarity can confuse similar but operationally distinct failures.

mistake: A new 768-dimensional embedding is queried against a 384-dimensional collection. Another index combines vectors from two model revisions with equal dimensions but incompatible geometry. Dimension checks catch only the first error.
takeaway: Use the vector calculator to compare cosine and raw dot rankings.

title: Embedding compatibility, batching and multilingual evaluation
objectives: Embedding compatibility, batching and multilingual evaluation
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects embedding compatibility, batching and multilingual evaluation with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Release evidence compares retrieval Recall@K and latency by query slice before and after re-embedding.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Equal vector dimensions do not imply compatible geometry. Two encoders can both produce 384 coordinates while mapping text into unrelated spaces. Mixing their document vectors or querying one index with the other encoder makes distance meaningless. Version the model revision, preprocessing, prefixes, pooling and normalization as one embedding contract.
Multilingual capability is a task requirement to test, not a property to infer from a model name. Error IDs and code snippets may also behave differently from natural-language paraphrases.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Batch text in a stable order with IDs, bound batch tokens and preserve per-item failures. Store a manifest beside each index generation. During an upgrade, build a new index, evaluate paired queries and switch atomically while retaining a compatible old generation for rollback.

For a query/document encoder, use the documented role prefixes. Evaluate exact codes, paraphrases, multilingual requests and ambiguous failure signatures. Check model revision and dimensions before issuing a query.
sections.code:
contract={'model':'encoder-a@revision','dimension':384,'normalize':True,'prefix':'document:'}
assert contract['dimension']>0

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A batch provider returns fewer vectors than inputs and the caller zips them silently, assigning later vectors to wrong IDs. An index upgrade changes normalization but keeps the old distance configuration. A cache reuses embeddings across preprocessing revisions.
Test cardinality, ID/order preservation, finite values, manifest equality and failed-item retry. Use separate cache keys for model and preprocessing contracts.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Release evidence compares retrieval Recall@K and latency by query slice before and after re-embedding. Report the cost of the full corpus migration and how long both indexes are retained.
SDETs should reject incompatible manifests deterministically before evaluating quality. A quality benchmark over mixed revisions cannot provide meaningful evidence about either encoder.

mistake: A batch provider returns fewer vectors than inputs and the caller zips them silently, assigning later vectors to wrong IDs. An index upgrade changes normalization but keeps the old distance configuration. A cache reuses embeddings across preprocessing revisions.
takeaway: Release evidence compares retrieval Recall@K and latency by query slice before and after re-embedding.

sections.title: Problem and intuition

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Retrieval-augmented generation supplies selected external evidence to a model at answer time. Ingestion loads, cleans, splits and versions documents; query-time retrieval selects context; generation produces an answer constrained by that context. RAG does not automatically prevent hallucination.

Chunking balances coherent evidence against retrieval specificity and context budget. Overlap can preserve cross-boundary facts but duplicates context. A heading-aware chunk should retain document ID, section, version, tenant and source offsets.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Context construction turns retrieved chunks into a bounded evidence package. Each chunk should carry an immutable evidence ID and enough source metadata for a citation to resolve. The answer must cite only supplied, authorized evidence; a plausible URL or title is not a valid provenance check.

A no-answer case is not a retrieval exception. The service may function correctly while no evidence supports the request. In that state, abstention is a valid outcome and should be present in the evaluation dataset.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Deduplicate overlapping chunks, reserve output/instruction tokens and pack evidence according to relevance and coverage. Use explicit evidence blocks with IDs; treat their text as untrusted data. After generation, validate cited IDs against the actual packed set, then evaluate whether the cited passage supports the claim.
These are two levels: deterministic resolution checks identity, while groundedness checks semantic support. Neither a resolved ID nor a high relevance score establishes every generated statement.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: The retriever finds the correct document, but context packing drops it. The model cites an ID remembered from an earlier session that was not supplied this turn. Another answer cites an authorized document that discusses the opposite rule.
Test unresolved IDs, empty context, conflicting evidence and revocation. Retain retrieval and packed-context IDs separately so the first failing stage can be identified.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The extractive baseline returns authorized source text with citations, visibly labeled as extractive rather than a live LLM answer. Live generation must meet the same provenance checks and an independently calibrated support rubric.
SDETs should report citation resolution, claim support and no-answer behavior separately. This makes a retrieval regression distinguishable from a hallucination or a context-budget defect.

title: Advanced retrieval: hybrid ranking and reciprocal rank fusion
objectives: Advanced retrieval
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions

relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects advanced retrieval: hybrid ranking and reciprocal rank fusion with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Incremental indexing needs freshness and deletion guarantees; Graph RAG represents relationships for multi-hop questions, while multimodal retrieval needs matching modalities and evidence provenance.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Sparse retrieval such as BM25 rewards lexical evidence including rare identifiers. Dense retrieval can recover paraphrases. Hybrid retrieval combines these complementary candidate lists. Reciprocal rank fusion scores a document by summing 1/(c+rank) across ranked lists, avoiding direct comparison of incompatible raw score scales.
A cross-encoder reranker scores query-document pairs with richer joint context, usually at greater latency. Retrieve enough candidates for recall, then rerank a bounded pool for precision.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Union sparse and dense IDs, compute reciprocal rank contributions, sort with a stable tie break and retain the top candidates. Apply permission filters in both retrieval paths and again before context construction. Reranking must never reintroduce forbidden candidates.

Query rewriting, multi-query retrieval and HyDE can expand recall, but generated rewrites can change intent. Parent-child retrieval returns precise child matches plus coherent parent context. Compression should preserve evidence required for the answer rather than summarize away a negation.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A dense query for HTTP 401 retrieves a semantically similar 403 guide but loses the exact error distinction. Conversely a lexical query for intermittent authentication fails to find a paraphrased expired-token document.

Run ablations for sparse, dense, fusion and reranking on the same queries. Inspect zero-hit, conflicting-evidence, multi-hop and tenant-isolation slices. Adding every technique without measuring its marginal value increases latency and debugging difficulty.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Incremental indexing needs freshness and deletion guarantees; Graph RAG represents relationships for multi-hop questions, while multimodal retrieval needs matching modalities and evidence provenance. These are architecture choices, not universal upgrades.

Use a retrieval-debug report showing candidate ranks at every stage. SDETs should identify whether a miss began in ingestion, candidate retrieval, fusion, reranking, context packing or generation before changing the prompt.

objectives: Freshness, deletion and incremental indexing

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A document store and its search index can diverge. Source deletion, permission revocation or a new version must propagate to retrieval before the service claims fresh authorized evidence. Incremental indexing updates changed records without rebuilding everything, but needs a consistent generation and deletion policy.
Freshness is a measurable lag between source change and serving visibility. A healthy database connection says nothing about whether the current index reflects required changes.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use source version, content hash, tenant and deleted status to compute an ingestion delta. Upsert stable IDs or replace the prior chunk set atomically; mark deleted records unavailable immediately and remove their vectors. Switch serving generations only after consistency checks.

A query trace records source/index versions. Permissions are revalidated at retrieval time so stale payloads cannot authorize a revoked document. Cache invalidation includes index generation and permission scope.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: New chunks are added but old chunks are never removed, producing contradictory answers. A tombstone is cleared accidentally when a retry replays an earlier ingest event. A source permission change fails to invalidate cached context.
Test update ordering, duplicate events, out-of-order versions, deletion/reingestion and permission revocation. Reject an older source version when a newer version is already committed.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Define and test a freshness SLO using synthetic updates and timestamps. Retain old compatible indexes for rollback while ensuring revoked content is blocked across every generation.

SDETs should inspect served IDs after changes rather than trusting ingestion success logs. A release passes only when updated/deleted evidence behaves correctly through the complete retrieval and cache path.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Precision@K is relevant retrieved documents divided by K; Recall@K is relevant retrieved documents divided by all relevant documents. Hit Rate measures whether any relevant item was found. MRR averages the reciprocal position of the first relevant result. NDCG compares discounted relevance gain with the ideal ranking and supports graded relevance.

Answer correctness and faithfulness are different: an answer can match external truth while making claims unsupported by supplied context. Conversely it can faithfully repeat an incorrect source. Test both against explicit evidence and gold expectations.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Build a golden dataset containing query, authorized tenant, relevant document IDs, reference claims and allowed abstention. Compute retrieval metrics before calling the generator. For graded labels, DCG=sum((2**rel-1)/log2(rank+1)); normalize by ideal DCG at the same cutoff.

Add deterministic checks for schema, resolved citations and forbidden actions. Use Ragas or DeepEval for semantic assessment with a configured evaluator, then calibrate it against human labels. Store judge model, prompt and rubric versions in the run artifact.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
