sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Binary relevance treats all useful documents equally. Graded relevance can distinguish a directly answering source from a partially useful source. DCG discounts later ranks because users and context budgets prioritize earlier evidence; NDCG divides observed gain by the best possible gain at the same cutoff.
A common gain function is 2^relevance−1, divided by log2(rank+1). The chosen grades, gain and cutoff are part of the metric definition. Comparing runs with different conventions is misleading.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: For relevance grades [0,3,1], the observed gain puts no benefit at rank one and large benefit at rank two. Sort the same candidate grades descending to calculate an illustrative ideal denominator. In a real benchmark, the ideal uses the full labeled relevant set at K, not merely the retrieved grades.
Handle an all-zero ideal explicitly, commonly returning zero. Preserve graded labels and reviewer guidance in the dataset so repeated evaluation uses the same relevance interpretation.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A scorer normalizes by the observed ranking itself, yielding one for every query. Another uses only retrieved items for the ideal and hides missing highly relevant documents. NDCG can improve while a required authorization invariant fails.
Test a perfect ranking, a swapped ranking, no relevance and missing high-grade evidence. Verify labels manually on a sample because precise arithmetic cannot repair bad relevance judgments.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An agent repeatedly selects actions based on observations and state. A deterministic workflow has transitions specified by the application; an agentic transition delegates some choice to a model. Use deterministic steps when inputs and required operations are known, and agentic selection when investigation requires choosing evidence paths.

State is the current task record, including goal, evidence, steps, budget and status. Memory is persisted information across steps or sessions; it needs scope and retention rules. A chat transcript alone is a poor substitute for explicit typed state.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Represent the loop with observe, decide, validate, authorize, execute and terminate stages. Each transition consumes a step and checks remaining wall-time and token budgets. Stop on goal completion, insufficient evidence, repeated action signatures or exhausted budget.

The automation assistant reads a failure, retrieves similar history and prepares a draft recommendation. Application code enforces allowed tools and approval, even when the model selects the next action. Persist a trace so a failed run can be replayed without repeating writes.

seen=set();budget=4
for action in ['read:F1','search:timeout','search:timeout']:

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An agent loops over the same unsuccessful search because its state lacks a record of tried queries. Another declares success after proposing a patch without checking the requested goal. These are state/termination failures, not merely bad wording.
Test repeated signatures, failed tools, missing observations, cancelled tasks and deadline expiry. Recovery may choose another permitted read, but it must not expand privileges or reset its budget.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply

objectives: Frameworks

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Frameworks package orchestration mechanisms; they do not define your quality contract. LangGraph exposes nodes, edges, shared state, conditional routing and persisted checkpoints. LangChain's current create_agent interface combines models and tools with standardized messages. LlamaIndex provides ingestion/retrieval abstractions for data-grounded applications.

Choose based on required control. A fixed classify-and-report pipeline needs little autonomous behavior. A resumable investigation with approval may benefit from a state graph. Keep domain validation outside framework-specific callbacks.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: The local graph lab declares typed state, adds read and draft nodes, connects START to read to draft to END, and invokes the graph on a synthetic failure ID. Conditional edges route insufficient evidence to review. A checkpointer persists state using a thread identity scoped to the user and tenant.

Interrupt before side effects, display the exact proposed action, then resume only with recorded approval. Parallel independent reads may merge results; define reducer semantics to avoid lost updates. Pin framework versions and run contract tests against upgrades.
sections.code:
from typing import TypedDict
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph,START,END
class State(TypedDict):
    failure_id:str
    draft:str
def draft(s):return {'draft':'Review '+s['failure_id']}
g=StateGraph(State);g.add_node('draft',draft)
g.add_edge(START,'draft');g.add_edge('draft',END)
app=g.compile()

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Model Context Protocol standardizes how hosts connect to servers exposing tools, resources and prompts. The host owns the user-facing application and policy; a client maintains a connection to a server. Tools perform operations, resources expose addressable context and prompts offer reusable interaction templates where supported.

MCP reduces bespoke integration wiring but does not make a server trustworthy. Tool descriptions and returned content are untrusted inputs; authentication identifies a party, while authorization determines which operation it may perform.

The client starts the server over stdio, initializes the session, lists tools and calls them with typed arguments. Streamable HTTP is a separate remote transport with its own authentication and session considerations.

Keep server stdout reserved for protocol messages in stdio mode; log to stderr. Validate IDs against a bounded fixture root and inject tenant from authenticated context rather than tool arguments. Expose read-only tools first.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Stdio connects a host to a locally launched server process through input/output streams. Streamable HTTP supports remote connections and introduces network identity, session and authentication considerations. Choosing a transport changes operational and security assumptions; it does not change the host's obligation to authorize tools.
A local fixture server can rely on a narrowly launched process with synthetic data. A remote deployment must protect its origin, audience, credentials, session lifecycle and downstream requests.

For a remote server, use the SDK's supported HTTP transport, enforce authenticated scopes and bind session handling to the intended client context.

Do not pass upstream bearer tokens to unrelated downstream services. Validate resource audiences and avoid treating arbitrary endpoint URLs from model text as trusted server configuration. TLS and authentication protect transport identity; authorization still restricts effects.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Deterministic checks enforce contracts with crisp truth conditions: JSON validity, enum membership, required fields, resolved citations, forbidden actions, latency and token budgets. Semantic checks assess correctness, relevance, completeness and groundedness against a rubric. Neither replaces the other.
A chatbot case can pass syntax while failing meaning, or answer correctly while violating privacy. Keep dimensions separate so release decisions reflect product risk rather than a convenient average.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A semantic judge rewards polished verbosity and misses an unsupported citation. An aggregate score gives a safety violation the same weight as a tone mismatch. A secret string appears in evaluator logs even though the user-facing answer was redacted.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An agent's result is only one part of its behavior. Component evaluation tests retriever, planner, model, tool and parser separately. Trajectory evaluation examines selected tools, argument correctness, unnecessary calls, loop behavior, permissions and progress toward the goal.

Two agents can produce the same correct summary while one reads unauthorized data. Goal completion and safe execution must both pass. Exact sequence matching may overconstrain valid alternative trajectories, so express essential actions and forbidden effects separately.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Store each trace event with task ID, step, tool, validated arguments, authorization result, output reference, duration and usage. Deterministic scorers count denied writes, duplicate signatures and budget violations. Evaluate goal evidence using explicit expected state.

Replay with fixture tools to isolate planning changes. Fault injection replaces one tool result with timeout, malformed data or an empty response. Compare whether the agent escalates, safely recovers or fabricates success.

violations=[e for e in trace if not e['authorized']]

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A benchmark accepts any final answer containing the word fixed even though no verification occurred. A trajectory scorer assumes read_failure must be the first call, rejecting an equally safe history-first strategy.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An evaluation framework turns cases into reproducible evidence. A case definition names task input, expected behavior, scorer configuration and thresholds. A runner invokes the system, captures output/trace, applies reusable scorers and creates a machine-readable verdict plus a human-readable report.
Dataset version, code revision, prompt/model configuration and execution mode are part of the run identity. Without them, a comparison cannot reliably explain a regression.

title: Security testing: injection, poisoning and tenant isolation
objectives: Security testing
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects security testing: injection, poisoning and tenant isolation with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Gate on zero unauthorized reads/writes and zero canary disclosure.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Prompt injection occurs when untrusted text attempts to redirect model behavior. Indirect injection arrives through retrieved documents, logs or tool results rather than the direct user request. Retrieval poisoning manipulates which evidence is selected; sensitive disclosure exposes data to an unauthorized audience.

These risks are connected but distinct. A document can be relevant yet malicious, or benign yet forbidden to the current tenant. Instructions to ignore prior rules are observable attack content; the enforceable boundary is application policy, not a promise that the model will ignore them.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism

title: Guardrails: layered validation and least privilege
objectives: Guardrails
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects guardrails: layered validation and least privilege with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The safe assistant can read fixtures and propose changes; actual writes require a matching unexpired action approval.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Guardrails are controls applied at specific boundaries: input validation, retrieval authorization, tool permissioning, output validation and rate limits. Moderation can classify content risks but cannot replace authentication or domain policy. Least privilege gives each component only the operations and data it requires.

Allowlisting provides a positive set of supported actions. Deny lists can supplement it for known attacks but are brittle as the primary permission mechanism. Human confirmation should approve a concrete action with scope and effect, not a vague intent.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Validate input size and types, derive identity from authentication, filter evidence before retrieval, restrict tool arguments and validate returned domain objects. Sandbox code candidates with bounded resources and no production credentials. Record policy decisions separately from model decisions.

An approval record includes action hash, principal, resource, expiry and status. Before execution, verify that the action still matches the approved payload and current permissions. Rate limits and anomaly checks bound abuse and accidental loops.

Test action mutation, expired approval, revoked access, oversized input and unknown tools. Review false positives by use case and ensure safe fallback or escalation is available when a guardrail blocks progress.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Model output is untrusted content. Returning JSON does not make embedded strings safe for HTML, logs, SQL or tools. Context-specific encoding prevents output from becoming executable markup, while authorization controls which facts or actions may be produced. Moderation is another classifier with false positives and false negatives.
A sensitive value may appear in logs or traces even when the final answer is redacted. Apply privacy rules across artifacts, not only the user-facing response.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Render text through React's escaped text nodes and sanitize generated SVG before insertion. Escape model/log text in HTML reports. Redact sensitive structured attributes recursively, and store permitted raw evidence only in a separate controlled location with retention rules.

Keep schema validation, domain evidence checks, content policy and output encoding separate. A moderation pass cannot authorize a cross-tenant read, and HTML escaping cannot make an unsupported factual claim correct.

assert html.escape('<script>')=='<script>'

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Generated tests are candidates that require independent validation. For GraphQL, inspect operations, arguments, required fields, nullability, enum values and authorization rules. A syntactically valid query may fail business rules; an HTTP 200 response may contain GraphQL errors.

Requirement traceability connects each candidate to the rule it tests. Count unique covered behaviors, not the number of generated files. Positive, negative, boundary, authentication and authorization cases should remain distinct.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Parse the schema and operation AST rather than splitting schema text with fragile string rules. Build a coverage matrix for required arguments, invalid enums, nullable/non-null fields, malformed operations and permission rules. Generate structured case definitions with expected data/errors.

For REST, use OpenAPI contracts and domain examples. For locator suggestions, validate candidates against the DOM and require uniqueness and stability. Regression selection uses dependency edges and historical risk; it must not exclude mandatory critical tests.

response={'data':None,'errors':[{'message':'Unauthorized'}]}

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A generated GraphQL test asserts only status 200 and passes when errors contains an authorization failure. A locator suggestion uses a dynamic index that happens to work once. Duplicate paraphrased cases inflate coverage statistics.

Compile/type-check candidates, execute against synthetic fixtures, inspect assertions and retain requirement IDs. Mutate a required field or expected value to prove the test can detect the intended failure.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply

title: Verify generated code: independent oracles and mutation checks
objectives: Verify generated code
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects verify generated code: independent oracles and mutation checks with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Candidate acceptance includes executable results, rejected mutations, reviewed dependencies and a human explanation of tradeoffs.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Generated code can import nonexistent APIs, mishandle edge cases or encode the wrong requirement. A compile/type check establishes basic structural compatibility, not correctness. Unit tests check isolated behavior; integration tests check real contracts; static and dependency checks address additional risks.
The model that wrote a function should not be the only authority judging it. Use independent requirements, trusted fixtures and known counterexamples as test oracles.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Run format/lint/type checks, targeted unit tests and integration tests in a sandbox before review. Inspect dependencies and API versions against official documentation. Keep secrets and production services unavailable to candidate code.

Mutation testing changes a relevant operator or return value and checks whether the suite fails. A surviving mutation reveals a possible assertion gap, though equivalent mutations need review. For a generated classifier, mutate category mapping and UNKNOWN handling.
sections.code:
def allowed(role):return role=='admin'

title: Production architecture: queues, cache and idempotent effects
objectives: Production architecture
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects production architecture: queues, cache and idempotent effects with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Architecture acceptance measures successful tasks under failure, not only normal throughput.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A production AI path includes authentication, admission control, retrieval, provider work, validation and response delivery. Caches reduce repeated work, queues decouple long tasks, circuit breakers limit calls to failing dependencies and fallbacks preserve a smaller safe capability. Each mechanism changes failure behavior and needs a contract.
Idempotency means repeating a request has the same intended effect as executing it once. A timeout is ambiguous: the remote system may have completed work even if the client received no response.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Key caches by tenant, permission scope, normalized request, prompt/model versions and index generation. Bound TTL and invalidate after permission or document changes. For side effects, persist an idempotency record before execution and return its existing result on duplicate requests.

A circuit breaker moves closed to open after configured failures, then half-open for limited probes after cooldown. Queued work has an expiry and cancellation path. Fallback answers must indicate reduced capability and retain the same authorization rules.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An open breaker routes to a backup provider with a different schema and the application treats arbitrary text as valid. A global cache returns another tenant's answer. A retry storm fills the queue faster than workers can drain it.
Inject provider outage, slow storage, duplicate requests and permission revocation. Check bounded queue growth, consistent duplicate results, visible degraded mode and eventual recovery.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Architecture acceptance measures successful tasks under failure, not only normal throughput. Document which dependency failures cause abstention, fallback or rejection.
SDETs should verify each transition with controlled faults and preserve traces for diagnosis. A retry mechanism is reliable only when it respects effect safety, capacity and deadlines.

title: Docker: reproducible images, non-root runtime and Compose
objectives: Docker
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects docker: reproducible images, non-root runtime and compose with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Deployment evidence includes the image build, API smoke tests and persistent-index restart test when that backend is enabled.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An image packages filesystem layers and runtime metadata; a container is an isolated running instance. Dockerfile layer order affects dependency cache reuse. Copying dependency manifests before application source lets source-only changes avoid reinstalling dependencies.

Containers improve reproducibility but do not automatically provide secure isolation, persistent data or correct service discovery. Secrets baked into layers can remain recoverable even if deleted later.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use a pinned base image policy, locked dependencies, a non-root user and a narrow build context. Set an explicit working directory, install dependencies before copying source and launch uvicorn on the container interface. Provide health/readiness endpoints and graceful shutdown.

Compose connects the API and optional Qdrant on an internal network with named persistent volumes. Keep provider secrets in runtime environment or secret mounts; exclude .env, caches and credentials with .dockerignore. Multi-stage builds can remove compilers from the final runtime.
sections.code:
# Dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
USER 10001
CMD ["uvicorn","app:app","--host","0.0.0.0","--port","8000"]

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: The service listens on 127.0.0.1 inside the container and is unreachable through a published port. A vector collection disappears after restart because no volume was attached. An image contains a copied .env.
Test build context, non-root identity, port reachability, health checks, volume persistence and stop behavior. Scan the image and verify dependency versions against the lockfile.

For an SDET, container tests are environment contract tests: the same synthetic request must behave consistently in the virtual environment and container, with configuration supplied externally.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A local import working in a virtual environment does not prove the container image works. Working directories, module paths, user permissions and dataset locations can differ. The shared service uses a configured dataset root so its domain code does not depend on the checkout's parent directory layout.
Build context determines which files are available to COPY. The repository-root context includes local-labs and datasets; a narrow fastapi-only context omits the shared quality package.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism

For Qdrant server mode, restart the service with its named volume and repeat an authorized query. Read-only API filesystems require temporary/runtime artifacts to use explicitly permitted storage rather than the image layer.

# From another terminal, probe /health, /ready and /chat

Test a known retrieval question inside the container, not merely process startup. Check shutdown, port mapping and persistence. If Docker is unavailable in the development environment, record that execution limitation instead of claiming a smoke pass.

objectives: CI/CD
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects ci/cd: ordered checks, artifacts and release gates with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The course integrity script is a required gate for missing phases, broken lesson references, absent checkpoints and invalid exercise schemas.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Continuous integration validates changes before they become release candidates. A useful pipeline installs locked dependencies, checks content and contracts, runs unit/integration tests, builds the app and executes representative browser and service tests. Continuous delivery packages a candidate after those gates; deployment publishes an approved artifact.
An AI quality report belongs in the gate sequence. Producing HTML without using its exit verdict does not protect a release.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use GitHub Actions jobs with explicit permissions, dependency caches and immutable artifacts. Run deterministic checks on every pull request. Live provider evaluations, when authorized and configured, use bounded datasets and protected secrets; forks must not receive those secrets.

Upload failure traces and evaluation reports using always() while keeping the job failed. Build GitHub Pages with the repository base path and test route reloads before publishing. Link the artifact to code, dataset and prompt revisions.

# CI command
python -m pytest local-labs
python local-labs/evals/runner.py --cases data/evaluation.json
npm run lint
npm test
npm run build

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A workflow appends || true to the evaluator and deploys despite hard-gate failures. A deployment rebuilds with different dependencies instead of publishing the tested artifact. A path filter skips tests when course JSON changes.
Test that deliberate content corruption and failing cases produce nonzero checks. Review workflow permissions and ensure deployment depends on the complete validation job.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The course integrity script is a required gate for missing phases, broken lesson references, absent checkpoints and invalid exercise schemas. Local evaluation returns a failing exit code for missing cases or violated invariants.
SDETs should demonstrate a red build from a known regression, then a green build after the fix. This proves that checks are connected to release behavior, not only documented.

title: GitHub Actions: failure artifacts and protected evaluation modes
objectives: GitHub Actions
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects github actions: failure artifacts and protected evaluation modes with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance includes a red gate that retained its artifacts and a corrected green gate using the same cases.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: CI should make failures reviewable. Unit results, browser traces, case reports and version manifests are artifacts that explain why a gate failed. Uploading them only on success loses the most useful evidence. Secret-bearing live evaluation requires a distinct protected execution context from forked contributions.
Deterministic fixture checks can run without credentials on every change. Live model-quality measurements should use configured budgets and stable cases, with mode prominently recorded.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Order install, content integrity, lint, unit/API checks, build and browser tests. Run the local evaluator and preserve its exit code. Upload reports with always() so a failed case still leaves its JSON/HTML evidence. Restrict workflow permissions to the job's actual needs.

Deploy the tested build artifact with the configured GitHub Pages base path. Content JSON changes must trigger validation just as code changes do. A separate completion-depth gate prevents structural validity from being mistaken for finished curriculum.
sections.code:
# Required local equivalents
npm run content:check
npm run lint
npm test
npm run build
python local-labs/evals/runner.py

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A workflow runs an evaluator but adds continue-on-error, making the release green. A fork is allowed to access provider secrets. A path filter runs only for src/**/*.tsx and skips broken lesson JSON.
Test the workflow logic with a known failing case and inspect that deployment cannot proceed. Review secret scope and artifact redaction, and record which checks were fixture-only versus live.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance includes a red gate that retained its artifacts and a corrected green gate using the same cases. Workflow YAML is a design artifact until its checks actually run in the intended environment.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: AI cost includes input/output tokens, embedding/indexing work, retries, agent steps, evaluation and human review. Price per token is only one input to cost per accepted task. Smaller models, shorter context and caching help only if they preserve the required outcome.
A routing policy sends simple cases to a low-cost path and escalates difficult or uncertain cases. Routing must be evaluated for false confidence, not merely average savings.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Set per-task and monthly budgets using dated provider rates. Track measured usage rather than estimating solely from characters. Cache authorized deterministic work and stable retrieval results, batch offline embedding jobs and reduce duplicate context.

Use confidence thresholds calibrated on held-out cases to route accepted classifications, uncertain cases to stronger analysis and unsupported cases to humans. Bound agent steps and judge calls as part of the same budget.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A task budget bounds total attempts and their resource use, not only the final accepted response. Retries, discarded generations, judge calls and agent tools all contribute. A request can stay within each component's local limit while exceeding the user's total allowance.

Estimates and measured usage serve different purposes. Reserve estimated capacity before work, then reconcile actual usage returned by the provider. Rates are dated configuration; this course does not embed current pricing as a permanent fact.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Track remaining input/output token allowance, call count, wall time and estimated currency cost in task state. Refuse or degrade before beginning work that cannot fit the budget. Include cached-token and reasoning usage according to provider accounting rather than guessing.

Calculate cost per accepted task over all attempts. Compare routing and caching variants on the same dataset with quality and privacy constraints held fixed. A low billed cost that increases wrong automated decisions is not a successful optimization.

remaining=1000
usage_events=[200,300,400]

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An agent gives each retry a fresh token limit and never reconciles total usage. A judge runs on every intermediate draft, multiplying spend. A cache uses tenant-free keys and saves cost by leaking evidence.

Test budget exhaustion before and after a provider response, duplicated retries and negative/invalid usage values. Ensure the visible status explains budget termination rather than claiming a completed investigation.

relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects performance tests: ttft, tails and realistic workloads with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Produce a load report with p50/p95/p99, TTFT, success rate, throughput and mode.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: TTFT measures time to the first generated token; end-to-end latency measures completion; tokens per second describes generation rate. p50, p95 and p99 summarize latency distributions. Throughput counts completed tasks per unit time, while concurrency counts in-flight tasks. These quantities answer different capacity questions.

title: Reliability: controlled faults and graceful degradation
objectives: Reliability
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects reliability: controlled faults and graceful degradation with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. A reliability report shows each injected fault, observed status, trace and invariant outcome.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Reliability is the ability to deliver an acceptable outcome despite dependency and input failures. AI failures include provider outage, rate limit, timeout, malformed result, hallucinated evidence, stale index, vector-store outage, broken tools, looping agents and context overflow. Not all failures should be retried.
Graceful degradation preserves a smaller truthful capability, such as displaying retrieved evidence without a generated explanation. It must be visible to the user and obey the same permissions.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Define a failure matrix with detection, retryability, fallback, user response and recovery evidence. Use deadlines, bounded retries, circuit breakers, index freshness checks, schema validation and step budgets. Record final status as successful, degraded, rejected or failed.

Inject one failure at a time in deterministic integration tests, then combine realistic correlated failures such as provider rate limits plus queue pressure. Ensure cancelled tasks release resources and duplicate requests cannot duplicate writes.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A fallback invents an explanation when retrieval is unavailable. A timeout handler retries indefinitely because each attempt resets the total deadline. A stale index passes health checks but returns deleted evidence.

Assert visible degraded status, no unsupported claims, bounded attempts and eventual recovery. Simulate both empty evidence and contradictory evidence, because hallucination defenses depend on more than transport errors.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: A reliability report shows each injected fault, observed status, trace and invariant outcome. Error budgets count user-visible failures over a specified window, with separate safety invariants that cannot be averaged away.
SDETs should make fault cases executable release checks, not a list of possible risks. The system passes when it behaves predictably under the failures it claims to tolerate.

mistake: A fallback invents an explanation when retrieval is unavailable. A timeout handler retries indefinitely because each attempt resets the total deadline. A stale index passes health checks but returns deleted evidence.
takeaway: A reliability report shows each injected fault, observed status, trace and invariant outcome.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A failure matrix names each dependency fault, detection signal, allowed recovery and visible result. Provider timeouts, malformed responses, retrieval absence and unsafe tool requests require different handling. Retrying everything treats deterministic invalidity as if it were transient.
Recovery must preserve the original trust boundary and budget. A fallback with broader access or unsupported claims turns a reliability mechanism into a security or quality regression.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Create one fixture per fault and assert final status, attempt limit, retained evidence and effects. The provider adapter uses an outer async deadline; the tool state machine stops repeated signatures; retrieval absence returns explicit abstention.

For combined faults, test shared capacity and cancellation. Recheck permissions and approvals after a resumed task. Keep error categories stable in the public API while retaining safe internal diagnostic references.

faults={'timeout':'unavailable','missing_context':'abstained','unsafe_write':'denied','loop':'stopped'}

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A malformed provider response is retried until the deadline but the public response still says success. A fallback copies another tenant's cached answer. A stopped agent's old partial draft is presented as a verified fix.
Inspect actual state and effect counts, not just error wording. Test that resources are released and that the next healthy request can succeed after the fault is removed.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance records each fault, expected and observed outcome, trace and recovery evidence. A declared tolerance is supported only by an executed case.

SDETs can run this suite without paid model calls by injecting the adapter/tool boundary. Live chaos experiments, when appropriate, add external-dependency evidence but do not replace deterministic recovery tests.

Rollback is a tested operation restoring a compatible set, not a prose instruction to use the old model. Permission revocations and deleted sources must remain enforced even when an older index generation is restored.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Write a manifest after gates pass, linking immutable hashes or revisions and the tested image. Register metrics and artifacts in MLflow or portable JSON. Preserve a rollback target and test a known fixture through that configuration.

Distinguish training artifacts from serving configuration and evaluator configuration. A provider may expose an alias rather than internal weights; record the alias, request date and observed behavior while acknowledging that limit.

Apply this mechanism to a synthetic incident in the shared fixture set. Preserve input/output identities so a reviewer can reproduce the result. Use the earlier lessons' implementation checks rather than assuming the checkpoint example is correct.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A model rollback retains the new label ordering and swaps categories. A prompt rollback retains an incompatible evidence schema. An older index exposes a document whose access was revoked after the index was built.
Test compatibility before switching traffic and apply current authorization at query time. Keep a manifest completeness check and a rollback smoke case in the release pipeline.

Construct a counterexample that fails the intended invariant, then describe how the same test would catch a future regression. State which layer owns the correction: data, numerical code, API validation, retrieval, policy or evaluation.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance includes manifest completeness, dataset/case identity, artifact compatibility and observed rollback behavior. Drift monitoring connects post-release failures to external provider or data changes.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Prompting changes instructions, RAG supplies changing evidence, and fine-tuning changes model parameters for repeated task behavior. Fine-tuning is not a reliable way to maintain rapidly changing facts or enforce authorization. Start with a baseline and a measured failure pattern before paying training and maintenance costs.

Supervised fine-tuning uses input/target examples. LoRA learns low-rank update matrices while keeping base weights frozen; PEFT is a broader family of parameter-efficient methods. These reduce trainable parameters, not the need for careful data and evaluation.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Create reviewed training examples with UNKNOWN and difficult classes, group related incidents to prevent leakage and reserve a held-out evaluation set. The optional local lab trains a tiny text classifier with torch; the PEFT example uses a configured public base checkpoint and LoRA adapter with explicit download/cost requirements.

Record base/tokenizer revisions, training hyperparameters, data hash and adapter artifacts. Compare against prompting and RAG baselines on accepted accuracy, calibration, safety, latency and total cost. Preserve source evidence outside weights.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Near-duplicate incidents appear in training and test, inflating accuracy. A fine-tuned model memorizes synthetic secret strings. Training loss falls while held-out performance declines, indicating overfitting.
Test deduplication and grouped splits, evaluate rare classes and check that unsupported requests still abstain. Red-team the adapted model and do not infer security from a lower training loss.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Choose adaptation only if held-out gains justify operational complexity. Report what improved, what regressed and how the adapter can be disabled or rolled back.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: LoRA parameterizes an update as low-rank factors rather than training every base weight. For an output-by-input matrix, factors with rank r use r times input+output trainable parameters. This reduces trainable state but does not prove better task behavior or reduce every inference cost automatically.

Initializing an adapter and running a forward pass are integration checks. Fine-tuning additionally optimizes it on reviewed examples, and acceptance additionally evaluates a held-out task and safety dataset.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: The optional PEFT script requires a chosen compatible public checkpoint and target projection names. It builds a sequence-classification adapter, checks output shape and saves the initialized adapter with an explicit untrained label. Use the real PyTorch training lab to understand optimizer, loss and holdout mechanics before extending the adapter script.

Record training examples, base/tokenizer revisions, rank, alpha, dropout and adapter artifact. Use grouped splits and compare prompting/RAG/baseline alternatives on the same independent evaluation cases.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: AI system design begins with users, tasks, failure costs and measurable constraints. A support chatbot, failure triage service, test-generation platform and enterprise RAG system share components but have different permissions, latency and quality requirements. State what the system may decide autonomously and what requires review.
A diagram is useful when it shows data flow, trust boundaries, state and failure paths. Boxes named LLM and database alone do not explain authorization, freshness, budgets or recovery.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Design the shared quality platform with authenticated API, typed domain services, retrieval, bounded agent tools, evaluation runner and report storage. Keep provider credentials server-side, tenant filters before retrieval and writes behind concrete approval.

Specify SLOs for latency, accepted accuracy and availability, plus hard invariants for privacy and tool effects. Plan cache scope, queue capacity, trace correlation, index updates and compatible rollback. Compare a deterministic baseline before adding autonomous orchestration.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A CI failure contains an exception, test identity, build context and history. The triage system must classify product, automation, environment, test-data or unknown causes without turning a plausible narrative into a confirmed defect. Similar failures provide evidence, not proof that two incidents share a root cause.
The portfolio result must be reproducible from the supplied synthetic fixtures and declared configuration. Keep a deterministic baseline visible alongside any live-provider results.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Build a grouped-split TF-IDF baseline, retrieve approved historical failures, then optionally ask a live model for a typed explanation with evidence IDs. Map probable owners from an explicit module registry rather than asking the model to invent a person. Export a report containing category, uncertainty, similar failures and review status.
The repository labs provide the domain entry points and fixture cases. Run the acceptance checks before recording project completion and keep the generated run ID in your field notes.
